106.s: The N.K. Singh FRBM Review Committee recommended which indicator as the principal fiscal anchor?
106.x: Debt-to-GDP was the principal anchor and fiscal deficit the operational target, with general government debt at 60% by 2023.
xa: Other recommendations: **FD 3% of GDP** for three years; **RD 0.8% of GDP by 2023**; an independent advisory **Fiscal Council**.
⚠ The new 2026-27 debt rule targets Central debt of **50 ± 1%** by **2031** — above FRBM's **40%**.
The **2018 amendment** set general govt **60%**, Centre **40%** by **31 March 2025**.

106.s: The debt anchor and escape-clause recommendations of the N.K. Singh Committee were incorporated into the FRBM Act through which amendment?
106.x: The committee's debt anchor and escape clause were written into the FRBM Act through the 2018 amendment.
106.tq: Match the substantive institutional change with the later amendment, not the amendment that added expenditure projections.
xs: The debt anchor and escape clause were written into the Act by the **2018 amendment** — option **(1)**.
2018 also set **FD 3% by 31 March 2021**, dropped RD/ERD targets and added a **buoyancy clause**.
**2012** added ERD and the MTEFS; **2015** deferred target dates — neither brought the debt anchor.
xa: 2018 debt anchor: general govt **60%**, Centre **40%** by **31 March 2025**.
The escape-clause deviation is capped at **0.5% of GDP**.
The Act is now cited as "**FRBM Act, 2003 (amended 2018)**".

106.s: The Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement sets ____ rolling targets.
106.x: It sets three-year rolling targets for revenue deficit, fiscal deficit, a tax-GDP indicator and total outstanding liabilities.
xa: MTFPS rolling targets have been **suspended since 2021-22** for post-pandemic flexibility.
**Budget 2026-27** laid a combined **MTFPS cum FPSS** with the **MEFS**.
The **Macro-Economic Framework Statement** covers growth, inflation, external balance and risks.

106.s: The 2018 amendment to the FRBM framework envisaged which combination of targets?
o: Fiscal deficit of 3% by 31 March 2021, general government debt of 60% and Central debt of 40% by 31 March 2025
Fiscal deficit of 3% by 31 March 2018 and Central debt of 50% by 2025
Fiscal deficit of 4.5% by 31 March 2025, general government debt of 50% and Central debt of 30% by 2031
Revenue deficit of zero and Central debt of 60% by 31 March 2021
106.x: The 2018 amendment set a 3% fiscal-deficit target by 31 March 2021 and debt anchors of 60% for general government and 40% for the Centre by 31 March 2025.
106.tq: Combine the year, date and multiple numerical targets without swapping their deadlines.
xs: The 2018 amendment set **FD 3% by 31 March 2021**, general govt debt **60%** and Central debt **40% by 31 March 2025** — option **(1)**.
It also dropped RD/ERD targets and added an **escape clause** (**0.5%** cap) and a **buoyancy clause**.
The **50%** Central debt by **2031** figure belongs to the new **2026-27** debt rule, not the 2018 amendment.
xa: The Government has acknowledged **deviation** from the Act's **3% FD** and **40% Central debt** targets.
COVID **2020-21**: FD **9.2%**; escape clause used, no amendment.

106.s: During COVID-19 in 2020–21, India's fiscal deficit was recorded at:
106.x: The fiscal deficit reached 9.2 per cent of GDP in 2020–21, after which targets were recalibrated with a gradual return path.
xa: The commitment to halve the 2020-21 FD in five years was met: **4.4% in 2025-26**.
In **2020-21** the escape clause was used with no amendment, to keep flexibility.

106.s: Which of the following is NOT a ground for invoking the FRBM escape clause?
o: Sharp fall in real output growth
Routine tax shortfall due to administrative delay
106.x: Grounds include national security, war, calamity, agricultural collapse, structural reforms and a sharp output fall, not routine administrative delays.
xa: Deviation limit: **not more than 0.5% of GDP** in a year.
The government must justify the deviation and give a return path, placed before **Parliament**.
⚠ Escape clause = deviation up to **0.5%**; buoyancy clause = FD cut of at least **0.25%**.

106.s:
Arrange the following FRBM developments in chronological order:
A. Targets suspended after the global financial crisis
B. Effective revenue-deficit target and Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement added
C. FRBM Rules notified and annual reduction targets introduced
D. Debt anchor, escape clause and buoyancy clause introduced through amendment
106.x: The sequence is 2004 Rules, 2008-09 suspension, 2012 additions, and 2018 amendment introducing the debt anchor and clauses.
106.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the 2008-09 and 2012 developments.
xs: Order: **C, A, B, D** — option **(1)**.
C: **2004** — FRBM Rules notified with annual reduction targets.
A: **2008-09** — targets suspended after the **global financial crisis**; B: **2012** — **ERD** and **MTEFS** added.
D: **2018** — **debt anchor**, escape clause and buoyancy clause.
xa: **2015**: target dates deferred (FD 3% by 2017-18).
**2020-21**: escape clause used for COVID; no amendment, to keep flexibility.
Rules in force from **5 July 2004**; Act enacted **2003**.

106.s: When the FRBM escape clause is invoked, the Government must place before Parliament:
o: An RBI approval for the deviation
A justification and a path back to the target
106.x: The Government must justify the deviation (capped at 0.5% of GDP) and lay a path back to the target before Parliament.
xa: Grounds: **national security, war, national calamity**, collapse of agriculture, **structural reforms**, severe slowdown.
Slowdown test: real output growth **3 percentage points** below the average of the previous four quarters.
⚠ **Buoyancy clause:** FD must fall by **at least 0.25%** if growth rises sharply.

106.s: The commitment to halve the 2020-21 fiscal deficit within five years was fulfilled when the fiscal deficit reached:
106.x: The 2020-21 fiscal deficit of 9.2% was more than halved to 4.4% in 2025-26. This was a commitment, not a legislative target.
106.tq: Calculate the direction of change while retaining the distinction between a commitment and a statutory target.
xs: The halving commitment was met when FD reached **4.4% of GDP in 2025-26** — option **(3)**.
**2020-21** FD was **9.2%**; halving it in five years was a commitment, **not a legislative target**.
xa: The **2025-26** target "below **4.5%**" (set in FY 2021-22) was met.
The **16th FC** path: Centre FD **3.5% of GDP by 2030-31**.

106.s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission described State fiscal rules as:
106.x: It called State fiscal rules 'effectively unenforced' and sought a wider deficit definition covering off-budget borrowing.
xa: **AP FRBM Act, 2005**: eliminate the revenue deficit; FD at **3% of GSDP**.

106.s: The FRBM escape clause can be triggered when real output growth falls ____ percentage points below the average of the previous four quarters.
106.x: One escape-clause trigger is a fall in real output growth by 3 percentage points below the average of the previous four quarters.
xa: Deviation under the escape clause: **not more than 0.5% of GDP** in a year.
Buoyancy clause: if growth rises sharply, FD must fall by **at least 0.25% of GDP**.

106.s: Under the buoyancy clause of the 2018 FRBM amendment, a sharp rise in real output growth requires the fiscal deficit to fall by at least:
106.x: The buoyancy clause requires at least a 0.25% of GDP cut in the fiscal deficit; it never permits an automatic increase.
xa: ⚠ Escape clause = deviation up to **0.5%**; buoyancy clause = FD cut of at least **0.25%**.
2018 also set the **debt anchor**: general govt **60%**, Centre **40%** by **31 March 2025**.

106.s: Under the Fifteenth Finance Commission, the net borrowing limit for States in 2022-23 was:
106.x: The limits were 4% in 2021-22, 3.5% in 2022-23, and 3% from 2023-24 to 2025-26 plus 0.5% for power-sector reforms.
xa: FRBM limits restrain AP's **open-market borrowing**.
AP slippage: FD **5.05%** vs mandated **4%** ceiling (7 Mar 2026).
**16th FC**: States **3% of GSDP** by **2030-31**.

106.s: Which one of the following correctly states the fiscal-deficit recommendations associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: Centre 3.5% of GDP and States 3% of GSDP by 2030-31
Centre 4.3% of GDP and States 3% of GSDP by 2026-27
Centre 3.5% of GDP and States 4% of GSDP by 2030-31
Centre 3% of GDP and States 3.5% of GSDP by 2030-31
106.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended that the Centre reach a fiscal deficit of 3.5% of GDP and States reach 3% of GSDP by 2030-31.
106.tq: Keep the Centre and State limits separate before comparing the two figures.
xs: The **16th FC**: Centre FD **3.5% of GDP** and States **3% of GSDP** by **2030-31** — option **(1)**.
**4.3%** is the Centre's FD in **2026-27 BE**, not an FC recommendation.
**4%** of GSDP was the **15th FC** State borrowing limit for **2021-22**.
xa: The 16th FC also asked for State fiscal-rule reform and a wider deficit definition covering **off-budget borrowing**.
It found State fiscal rules "**effectively unenforced**".
⚠ FRBM 2018 target for the Centre was **3%**; the 16th FC path is **3.5%** by 2030-31.

106.s: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act enacted?
106.x: The AP FRBM Act was enacted in 2005; it aims to eliminate the revenue deficit and limit the fiscal deficit to 3% of GSDP.
xa: It has been amended from time to time to match **Finance Commission** borrowing limits.
**AP BE 2026-27**: FD **3.84%**, RD **1.11%** of GSDP — above the **3%** norm.
Slippage: FD **5.05%** vs mandated **4%** ceiling; borrowings **₹81,071 crore**.

106.s: State fiscal responsibility legislation was promoted after the Twelfth Finance Commission because debt relief was linked to:
o: The Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility
The Goods and Services Tax Compensation Fund
106.x: The Twelfth Finance Commission linked debt relief for States to the enactment of fiscal responsibility legislation through the Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility.
106.tq: Identify the specific facility associated with the debt-relief incentive.
xs: The **12th FC** tied debt relief to the **Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility** — option **(1)**.
States enacted Fiscal Responsibility Legislation mostly after this link.
Several States passed FRBM Acts on the **central model**; AP's came in **2005**.
xa: AP FRBM Act targets: eliminate RD, **FD 3% of GSDP**.
The central FRBM Act does **not apply to States**.
**16th FC** found State fiscal rules "**effectively unenforced**".

106.s: The main significance of the FRBM framework is that it:
o: Made fiscal discipline a legal duty and added disclosure statements to the Budget
Gave the Finance Commission control over Union borrowing
106.x: The FRBM framework gave fiscal discipline a legal basis and made disclosure statements part of the Budget process.
xa: Criticism: frequent **escape-clause** use and repeated target deferrals.
Design gaps: **no penalty clause**; no independent **fiscal council** yet.
Current relevance: Budget 2026-27 switched to a debt-GDP rule (**50 ± 1% by 2031**).

106.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBM Act)?
o: It concerns both fiscal and revenue deficit
It concerns neither fiscal deficit nor revenue deficit
106.x: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003 is a landmark Indian legislation aimed at institutionalizing financial discipline, reducing the fiscal deficit, eliminating the revenue deficit, and managing public debt. It compels the government to adopt transparent budgetary practices to ensure long-term macroeconomic stability and inter-generational equity.

106.s: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act was enacted in India in the year :
106.x: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003 was enacted in August, 2003. It became effective from 5 July, 2004 (date of commencement). The FRBM Act, 2003 sets a target for the Government to establish financial discipline in the economy, improve the management of public funds, reduce the fiscal deficit and improved macroeconomic management by moving towards a balanced budget and strengthen financial prudence. The FRBM Act, 2003 requires the Central Government to progressively reduce its outstanding debt, revenue deficit and fiscal deficit. The Central Government has to give threeyear rolling targets for these indicators when it presents the Union Budget each year. The Government was supposed to achieve fiscal deficit of 3% of GDP by 31 March, 2021. In Budget Estimates 2020-21, the fiscal deficit target was relaxed to 3.5% (as permitted by the FRBM Act) and it was estimated that fiscal deficit of 3.1% will be achieved by 2022-23, but as per actual figures of 2020-21, the fiscal deficit was zoomed to 9.2% of GDP (due to COVID-19 pandemic impact). It is to be noted that the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement has not provided rolling targets for budget deficits since 2021-22. The Union Government in Budget Speech of FY 2024-25 has outlined a medium term policy stance. It seeks to keep the central Government fiscal deficit to GDP ratio such that the debt to GDP ratio is on a declining path from 2026-27 onwards.

106.s: Along with the budget, the Finance Minister also places other documents before the parliament which include "The Macro Economic Framework Statement" The aforesaid document is presented because this is mandated by
o: Article 112 and Article 110(1) of the constitution of India
Article 113 of the Constitution of India
Provisions of the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003
106.x: The documents that the government is required to present along with the budget as per the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 are: Macroeconomic Framework Statement: This statement provides an overview of the economy, including GDP growth, inflation, receipts and expenditure.  Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement: This statement sets out the government's fiscal policy goals for the medium term.  Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement: This statement explains how the government plans for fiscal policy goals.  Medium-Term Expenditure Framework: This framework sets out the government's spending plans for the medium term.

106.s: Along with the Budget, the Finance Minister also places other documents before the Parliament which include 'The Macro Economic Framework Statement'. The aforesaid document is presented because this is mandated by :
o: Article 112 and Article 110 (1) of the Constitution of
Article 113 of the Constitution of India
Provisions of the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget
106.x: Every year, along with the budget, the 'Macro-Economic Framework Statement' is presented before the Parliament by the Finance Minister. This is mandated under provisions of section 3 of the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003. The statement contains an overview of the economy. This includes an assessment regarding the GDP growth, fiscal balance of the central government and the external sector balance of the economy.

106.s:
Consider the following statements :
Assertion (A) : There is a history of fiscal deficit in Central Government budgets in India.
Reason (R) : Indian agriculture has enjoyed large amount of subsidies compared to Western countries.
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct
106.x: There is a history of fiscal deficit in Central Government budgets in India. Hence, Assertion (A) is correct.While Reason (R) is wrong because India's subsidies to its agriculture sector are quite low as compared to Western countries. So option (c) is correct answer.

107.s: Along with the end of the Plan/non-Plan classification, the Union Budget began to be presented on:
107.x: The Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget and the Budget was presented on 1 February.
xa: ⚠ **2017** = three changes together: **Railway merger** + **1 February** date + **plan/non-plan** ended.
The separate Railway Budget had run from **1924** (**Acworth Committee**, 1921) — a **92-year** practice ended.
The plan/non-plan split was removed on the advice of the **Expenditure Management Commission**.

107.s: The separate Railway Budget was introduced in 1924 on the recommendation of the:
107.x: The separate Railway Budget began in 1924 following the recommendations of the Acworth Committee constituted in 1921.
107.tq: Match the reform with the committee that recommended it.
xs: The separate Railway Budget began in **1924** on the **Acworth Committee** (**1921**) recommendation — option **(2)**.
It was merged with the Union Budget in **2017** (Budget 2017-18), ending a **92-year** practice.
The **Expenditure Management Commission** is linked to ending the plan/non-plan split, not the Railway Budget.
xa: The Budget date also moved to **1 February** in **2017**.
**Outcome Budget / Gender Budget** came in **2005-06**; the Budget went **paperless** in **2021**.

107.s: India's Budget has been presented in paperless or digital form since:
107.x: The Budget has been presented in paperless or digital form since 2021.
107.tq: Recall the starting year of the digital reform.
xs: The Budget has been **paperless (digital)** since **2021** — option **(4)**.
**2017** is the year the Budget moved to **1 February** and the Railway Budget merged.
**2019** is when **Nirmala Sitharaman** began presenting every Budget.
xa: Printing begins with the **Halwa ceremony** at **North Block**.
The word "Budget" comes from French **bougette** ("little bag") and is **not in the Constitution**.

107.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Liaquat Ali Khan – Presented the most budgets (10)
James Wilson – First budget of India, 7 April 1860
R.K. Shanmukham Chetty – First budget of independent India, 26 November 1947
107.x: Liaquat Ali Khan presented the 1947-48 Interim Government budget; Morarji Desai presented the most budgets (10).
xa: **Nirmala Sitharaman** has presented every Budget since **2019**.
The Budget date moved to **1 February** in **2017**.
**1973-74** = "Black Budget"; **1997-98** = "Dream Budget".

107.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Receipt Budget — output-outcome framework for schemes
Expenditure Profile — detailed estimates of tax receipts
Outcome Budget — output-outcome framework for schemes
107.x: The Outcome Budget presents the output-outcome framework for schemes. The Receipt Budget deals with receipts, while the Expenditure Budget or Expenditure Profile deals with spending.
107.tq: Start from the sure document-function pair and eliminate swapped descriptions.
xs: **Outcome Budget — output-outcome framework for schemes** is correct — option **(3)**.
The **Receipt Budget** gives estimates and trends of tax, non-tax and capital receipts — so option (1) is wrong.
The **Expenditure Profile** is scheme- and ministry-wise **spending**; the **Finance Bill** carries **tax proposals**.
xa: **Appropriation Bill**: **Art. 114(3)** — authorises withdrawal from the CFI.
**Finance Bill** is under **Art. 110(1)(a)**, with an explanatory **Memorandum**.
Other documents: **Budget at a Glance**; FRBM statements (**MEFS**; **MTFPS cum FPSS**).

107.s: The word 'Budget' comes from the French word 'bougette', meaning:
107.x: 'Bougette' means 'little bag'; Budget printing begins with the Halwa ceremony at North Block.
xa: The **Budget circular** is issued in **September**.
The Budget is prepared by the **Budget Division, Department of Economic Affairs**, Ministry of Finance.

107.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the Appropriation Bill?
107.x: Article 114 covers the Appropriation Bill; 112 is the Annual Financial Statement, 113 the estimates, 115 supplementary grants.
xa: **Art. 116** = **vote on account**, vote of credit, exceptional grants; **Art. 117** = special provisions on financial bills.

107.s: Who prepares the Union Budget through the Budget Division?
o: NITI Aayog independently of the Ministry of Finance
Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
107.x: The Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs in the Ministry of Finance prepares the Union Budget, in coordination with NITI Aayog and spending ministries.
107.tq: Apply the ‘who performs this job?’ test to distinguish adjoining financial institutions.
xs: The Budget is prepared by the **Budget Division, Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance** — option **(2)**.
It works with **NITI Aayog** and the spending ministries — NITI does not prepare it independently.
The **Department of Revenue** (**CBDT/CBIC**) only furnishes revenue estimates.
xa: The DEA also prepares budgets of **States under President's Rule** and **UTs**.
The **Budget circular** is issued in **September**; printing begins with the **Halwa ceremony** at **North Block**.

107.s: The Annual Financial Statement is provided for under Article:
107.x: Article 112 provides for the Annual Financial Statement; the Constitution does not use the word 'Budget'.
xa: The AFS is presented on the "**first working day of February**" — in practice **1 February**, even on a Sunday (**2026**).
The **Contingency Fund of India** (Art. 267) corpus was raised to **₹30,000 crore** from **2021-22**.

107.s:
Assertion (A): Demands for Grants include revenue expenditure, capital expenditure and loans.
Reason (R): Charged expenditure is not shown separately in the Demands for Grants.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
107.x: A is true: Demands for Grants (Article 113) cover revenue, capital and loan components. R is false: charged items are shown separately.
xa: Demands are voted **only by Lok Sabha** and need the **President's recommendation**.
**Guillotine**: on the last allotted day, remaining demands are put to vote **without discussion**.
Cut motions: **policy cut ₹1**; **token cut ₹100**; economy cut by a stated amount.

107.s: A Finance Bill is treated as a Money Bill under which constitutional provision?
107.x: A Finance Bill comes within the scope of a Money Bill under Article 110(1)(a), insofar as it contains provisions dealing with taxation.
107.tq: Distinguish the constitutional provision governing taxation-related Money Bills.
xs: The Finance Bill is a **Money Bill** under **Article 110(1)(a)** — option **(2)**.
It gives effect to the **tax proposals** and comes with an explanatory **Memorandum**.
**Art. 112** is the **Annual Financial Statement**, not the Finance Bill.
xa: The Finance Bill must be enacted within **75 days** (**Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931**).
It is the **sixth** and last stage of the budget process, after the **Appropriation Bill**.

107.s: The Public Account of India is provided for under Article:
107.x: The Public Account is under Article 266(2); withdrawals need no appropriation since the government acts only as banker.
xa: **Art. 266** = Consolidated Fund; **Art. 267** = Contingency Fund.
The **Contingency Fund** corpus was raised to **₹30,000 crore** from **2021-22**.

107.s: The list of expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India is laid down in:
107.x: Article 112(3) lists charged expenditure (President's emoluments, debt charges, judges' salaries, CAG etc.). Art 114(3) bars withdrawal from the CFI without an Appropriation Act, Art 266(2) is the Public Account, and Art 110(1)(a) brings tax provisions within a Money Bill.
107.tq: Charged list = 112(3); discussable but not votable = 113(1).
xs: Charged expenditure is listed in **Article 112(3)** — option **(1)**.
**Art. 114(3)** bars withdrawal from the CFI without an **Appropriation Act**.
**Art. 266(2)** is the **Public Account**; **Art. 110(1)(a)** is the **Finance Bill**.
xa: Charged items include the **President**'s emoluments, **debt charges**, **SC judges**' salaries, the **CAG**.
Charged expenditure is **not voted**, only **discussed** (**Art. 113(1)**).

107.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its budget-account characteristic?
o: Capital account — current-year routine transactions only
Capital account — no transactions involving liabilities
Revenue account — creation of long-term assets only
107.x: The revenue account records current-year transactions, while the capital account relates to assets and liabilities.
107.tq: Use the running-versus-asset-creation distinction to reject reversed descriptions.
xs: **Revenue account — current-year transactions** is correct — option **(3)**.
The **capital account** records **assets and liabilities**, so options (1) and (2) are wrong.
Revenue spending **creates no asset** — it maintains assets (salaries, pensions, interest, subsidies).
xa: Capital spending creates assets or reduces liabilities: capex, roads, **defence equipment**, loans given, debt repayment.
Mnemonic: "Revenue = Running the government; Capital = Creating assets".

107.s: Which of the following gives effect to the tax proposals of the Union Budget?
107.x: The Finance Bill gives effect to tax proposals; the Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund.
xa: The Finance Bill must be enacted within **75 days** (**Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931**).
The **Public Account** needs no appropriation — the government acts as banker.

107.s: Under the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931, the Finance Bill must be enacted within:
107.x: The Finance Bill must be enacted within 75 days under the stated provision of the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931.
107.tq: Recall the statutory time limit using closely spaced numerical options.
xs: The Finance Bill must be enacted within **75 days** — option **(3)**.
This comes from the **Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931**.
The Finance Bill is a **Money Bill** under **Art. 110(1)(a)** and gives effect to tax proposals.
xa: Budget = estimate statement; **Finance Bill** = the legal instrument for taxes.
The Finance Bill comes with an explanatory **Memorandum**.

107.s: No money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India without:
107.x: Withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund (Article 266) needs an Appropriation Act; a vote on account authorises advance spending.

107.s: A full statement of receipts and expenditure presented by an outgoing government in an election year is called:
107.x: An interim budget is a full statement of receipts and expenditure by an outgoing government; a vote on account only authorises expenditure for part of the year.
xa: In election years a vote on account covers **3-5 months**.
⚠ Vote on account is rarely needed since **1 February**, except in **interim budget** years.

107.s: A government has a fiscal deficit of Rs 80,000 crore and interest payments of Rs 25,000 crore. Its primary deficit is:
107.x: Primary deficit equals fiscal deficit minus interest payments. Therefore, it is Rs 80,000 crore minus Rs 25,000 crore, or Rs 55,000 crore.
107.tq: Apply the primary-deficit formula and subtract interest payments from fiscal deficit.
xs: Primary deficit = **Rs 55,000 crore** — option **(3)**.
Formula: **PD = FD - interest payments** = Rs 80,000 crore - Rs 25,000 crore.
**Rs 80,000 crore** is the FD itself; **Rs 1,05,000 crore** wrongly adds interest.
xa: **FD** = total expenditure - receipts excluding borrowings.
**RD** = revenue expenditure - revenue receipts.
Interest takes **20** paise of every rupee spent in 2026-27.

107.s: Voting on Demands for Grants takes place in:
o: A joint sitting of both Houses
107.x: General discussion is in both Houses, but Demands for Grants are voted only in the Lok Sabha.
xa: Demands need the **President's recommendation**.
**Guillotine**: remaining demands put to vote **without discussion** on the last allotted day.

107.s: The combined fiscal deficit of the States in FY25 rose to:
107.x: It rose to 3.2 per cent in FY25; 18 States exceeded the 15th FC's 3 per cent limit in FY24.
xa: Union FD for comparison: **4.3%** of GDP in **2026-27 BE**.
AP: CAG flagged its **revenue deficit** for three years.

107.s: Which of the following is an example of charged expenditure?
107.x: Interest on public debt is charged expenditure: non-votable but discussable, and shown separately in appropriation.
xa: Charged expenditure comes **straight from the Consolidated Fund**.

107.s: The salaries of the CAG and UPSC members are charged expenditure, which means they are:
107.x: Charged expenditure, such as for presiding officers, UPSC and CAG, is discussable but not voted.
xa: Also charged: **President**'s emoluments, **debt charges**, **SC judges**' salaries and pensions.

107.s: Cut motions on the Budget are moved at the stage of:
107.x: Cut motions come at the voting on demands; the general discussion has no cut motions or voting.
xa: Six stages: presentation → general discussion → **DRSC** scrutiny → voting on demands → **Appropriation Bill** → **Finance Bill**.
**Voting on demands** (**Art. 113**) is **only in Lok Sabha**.

107.s:
Arrange the following stages of the Union Budget process in the correct chronological order:
A. Voting on Demands for Grants
B. Presentation of the Budget
C. Finance Bill
D. General discussion
107.x: The sequence is presentation, general discussion, voting on Demands for Grants and then the Finance Bill, with the Appropriation Bill preceding the Finance Bill.
107.tq: Fix the first and last stages, then place discussion and voting between them.
xs: Order: **B, D, A, C** — option **(1)**.
**Presentation** → **general discussion** → **DRSC scrutiny** → **voting on demands** → **Appropriation Bill** → **Finance Bill**.
The **Finance Bill** is the **last** stage, after the Appropriation Bill.
xa: General discussion: both Houses, **3-4 days**; no cut motions.
Voting on demands (**Art. 113**): **only Lok Sabha**.
Finance Bill must be enacted within **75 days**.

107.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Performance budget – Expenditure without reference to results
Outcome budget – Control over individual items of expenditure
Zero-based budget – Traditional control over individual items of expenditure
Line-item budget – Traditional control over individual items of expenditure
107.x: A line-item budget is the traditional budget focused on control over individual items of expenditure.
xa: **Zero-based** budgeting justifies every activity afresh from zero (**Peter Pyhrr**).
**Outcome** budgeting tracks outputs and outcomes, not outlays (from **2005-06**).

107.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
o: President’s emoluments; interest on public debt; salary and office expenses of the CAG
Salaries of all Members of Parliament; grants to States; election expenditure
All Demands for Grants; salaries of ministers; public debt receipts
Finance Commission grants; subsidies; salaries of all government employees
107.x: The President’s emoluments, interest on public debt, and the salary and administrative office expenses of the CAG are charged expenditure. The other sets contain items not identified as charged expenditure here.
107.tq: Use elimination by checking whether every item belongs to the charged category.
xs: **President's emoluments; interest on public debt; salary and office expenses of the CAG** — all charged — option **(1)**.
Charged items also include salaries of RS **Chairman/Deputy Chairman** and LS **Speaker/Deputy Speaker**, and **UPSC** chairman/members.
**Court decrees/awards** and anything **Parliament declares charged by law** are also charged.
xa: Basis: **Art. 112(3)**; charged items are **not voted**, only discussed.
⚠ **SC judges** = salaries + pensions charged; **HC judges** = only **pensions** charged.

107.s: Which of the following is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
107.x: Salaries, allowances and pensions of Supreme Court judges, and pensions of High Court judges, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
xa: Other charged items: **President**'s emoluments, **CAG**'s salary, **UPSC**, **debt charges**.

107.s: In parliamentary financial procedure, the guillotine refers to
o: putting all outstanding demands to vote without discussion on the last day
the automatic rejection of all demands for grants
the President's power to withhold assent to a Money Bill

107.x: Zero-based budgeting (ZBB) is a method of budgeting in which all expenses must be justified for each new period. Zero-base budget technique involves a critical review of every scheme before a budgetary provision is made. Developed by Peter Pyhrr in the 1970s, zero-based budgeting starts from a ‘zero base’ at the beginning of every budget period, and every function within an organization is analyzed for its needs and costs. Jimmy Carter, then Governor of Georgia (U.S.), was the first to adopt the process of zero-base into the government in 1973 budget. Three years later, the U.S. federal government for the first time implemented zero-based budgeting in ‘The Government Economy and Spending Reform Act, 1976’. In India, the Department of Science and Technology was the first to introduce zero-based budgeting in 1983 and in 1986, the Indian Government adopted zero-based budgeting for determining expenditure budget.

Identify the correct sequence in the classification of government receipts:
A. Revenue Receipts
B. Capital Receipts
C. Tax Revenue
D. Non-tax Revenue Note: For this question, discrepancy is found in question/answer. So,this question is ignored for all candidates.

Consider the following statements :
I. Capital receipts create a liability or cause a reduction in the assets of the Government.
II. Borrowings and disinvestment are capital receipts.
III. Interest received on loans creates a liability of the Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Government receipts are divided into two main categories– Revenue Receipts and Capital Receipts. Th ose government receipts which create a liability for the government or reduce its fi nancial assets are called Capital Receipts. On the other hand, Revenue Receipts, are those which neither create any additional liability on the government nor reduce its assets; these include tax revenue and non-tax revenue (such as interest, dividend, fees, etc.). When the government borrows from the market, RBI, or other financial institutions, it creates an obligation to repay the principal and interest in the future; therefore, these receipts create a new liability for the government and are treated as Capital Receipts. Under Disinvestment, the government sells its equity stake in public sector enterprises. This reduces the government’s financial assets, and in official accounting such receipts are also treated as Capital Receipts (especially as non-debt capital receipts). Thus, both borrowings and disinvestment are capital receipts. The interest received by the Central Government on loans given to states, public sector enterprises, etc., is classified officially as non-tax revenue and included under Revenue Receipts, not under Capital Receipts. Revenue receipts neither create any new liability nor reduce the government’s financial assets. Thus, only Statements I and II are correct, while Statement III is incorrect; therefore, the correct answer is option (a).

110.x: As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, Per Capita Annual Income in India in the year 1991-92 was at Rs. 6835 at current prices. Thus the nearest correct answer is option (c). According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, Per Capita Income at current and constant (2011-12) prices in 2025-26 (1st A.E.) was at Rs. 219575 and Rs. 121968, respectively.

110.s: Statement A: All India Per Capita Income for 2023-24 (PE) is estimated at Rs.1,84,205. Statement B: This is lower than the Andhra Pradesh Per Capita Income for 2023-24 (AE).
o: Both statements A and B are correct
Both statements A and B are incorrect
110.x: As per provisional national accounts estimates, the All-India per capita income (at current prices) for 2023-24 was around Rs. 1,84,205. Andhra Pradesh's per capita income for the same year, per its state economic survey, was estimated higher than the national average, since AP is traditionally among the higher per-capita-income major states. Hence both statements are correct.

110.s:
According to the report on Relative Economic Performance of Indian States (1960-61 to 2023- 24) by the Economic Advisory Council to the PM, Ele
(1)
(2) what are the individual shares of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana in the National GDP in FY 2023- 24?
110.x: The EAC-PM report on the Relative Economic Performance of Indian States found that Telangana, with its stronger urban / service and industrial base centred around Hyderabad, has a somewhat higher share of national GDP than Andhra Pradesh, with the report estimating AP's share at around 4.5% and Telangana's share at around 5.1% for FY 2023-24.

110.s: Which state has the largest economy in India ?
110.x: With reference to the year 2023–24, at constant (2011–12) and current prices, Maharashtra is the state with the largest economy in the country. According to the Economic Survey 2025–26, the Net State Domestic Product (NSDP) at current prices (in crore rupees) of the given states in 2023-26 is as follows – State NSDP at Current Prices (in crore Rs.) Maharashtra 3537968 Gujarat 2167160 Tamil Nadu 2412414 Uttar Pradesh 2308320

110.s: Which of the following States has highest Per Capita Average Income?
110.x: As per the question period, the Per Capita Income of Haryana was maximum among the given States. As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, Per Capita Income (NSDP Per Capita at current prices) of these States for the year 2023-24 are as follows : Karnataka (Rs. 339813), West Bengal (Rs. 149515), Haryana (Rs. 319363) and Gujarat (Rs. 300957). Hence, as per the latest available data, Karnataka has the highest Per Capita NSDP among the given States.

110.s: Which of the following States has the highest Per Capita Income (at present) ?
110.x: As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, in 2023-24, the Per Capita Income (NSDP Per Capita) of Goa (Rs. 585953) was highest among the given States. Goa has the second highest NSDP Per Capita after Sikkim among all States in 2023-24.

110.s:
Arrange the following States in descending order of Per Capita Income for the year 1998-99 and select the correct answer from the codes given below:
A. Maharashtra
B. Gujarat
C. Uttar Pradesh
D. Punjab
110.x: Option (b) was the correct answer for the question period. As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, Per Capita Net State Domestic Product at current prices of the above States (As on 1 August, 2025), is as follows : State Per capita NSDP (in Rs.) 2022-23 2023-24 Punjab 185802 205374 Maharashtra 252289 278681 Gujarat 269983 300957 Uttar Pradesh 84640 97365 Hence, as per the data of year 2022-23 and 2023-24, the descending order of these States is BADC.

110.s:
Consider the following States:
1. Gujarat
2. Karnataka
3. Maharashtra
4. Tamil Nadu The descending order of these States with reference to their Per Capita Net State Domestic Product is:
110.x: As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, the Per Capita Income (NSDP Per Capita) of Bihar at current prices is Rs. 62201 in 2023-24, which is lowest among all States in India. The Per Capita Income of Sikkim (Rs. 587743) is highest in the country in 2023-24.

111.s: Which of the following correctly represents the area of residual Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation, as given in the relevant data?
o: 1,62,970 sq km from the date of bifurcation
1,60,205 sq km, later revised to 1,62,970 sq km
111.x: Residual Andhra Pradesh had an area of 1,60,205 sq km, subsequently shown as 1,62,970 sq km. Telangana covers 1,12,077 sq km.
111.tq: Use the exact area figures and distinguish the original and revised values.
xs: Residual AP had **1,60,205 sq km**, later revised to **1,62,970 sq km** — option **(4)** is correct.
The rise came from **7 Khammam mandals** moved to AP for **Polavaram**.
**1,12,077 sq km** is **Telangana**; **2,75,000 sq km** is undivided AP; 1,62,970 was not the figure from the date of bifurcation.
xa: Population (Census 2011): AP **4.96 crore**, Telangana **3.52 crore**.
APRA population ratio: **58.32 : 41.68**.
Telangana is **landlocked** — AP kept the **entire coastline**.

111.s: According to the 2011 Census, the population of residual Andhra Pradesh was about:
111.x: Residual Andhra Pradesh had 4.96 crore people and Telangana 3.52 crore; the APRA population ratio was 58.32:41.68.
xa: Central Generating Station power: AP (**58%** population) got only ≈ **46%**.
Undivided AP ≈ **2,75,000 sq km**.

111.s: After the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, which State retained the entire coastline and all the ports of the undivided State?
o: Both Andhra Pradesh and Telangana equally
111.x: Telangana is landlocked; therefore, residual Andhra Pradesh retained the entire coastline and all the ports of the undivided State.
111.tq: Use the geographical condition to identify the State retaining the coastal assets.
xs: **Residual Andhra Pradesh** kept the **entire coastline** and **all ports** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Telangana is landlocked**, so it got no coast.
xa: Ports: **Visakhapatnam, Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, Kakinada, Machilipatnam**.
Coastline: **1,053.07 km**, **3rd longest** (after Gujarat, Tamil Nadu).
AP kept the coast, deltas and Krishna-Godavari tail-end; lost **coal** + Hyderabad industrial base.

111.s: After the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, coal resources went mainly to:
111.x: Coal went mainly to Telangana, while residual Andhra Pradesh retained important coastal and basin minerals.
xa: AP called "**Ratna Garbha**" for its minerals.
AP's minor coal: **Godavari valley belt** (East/West Godavari, ASR).
SCCL's existing coal linkages for AP plants continue (**Twelfth Schedule**).

111.s: Mangampet in YSR Kadapa district has India's largest deposit of:
111.x: Mangampet has India's largest barytes deposit; Tummalapalle (YSR Kadapa) is AP's uranium site and AP's bauxite is in Araku, Chintapalli and Paderu.
xa: Coal went mainly to **Telangana**.
Limestone: AP **3rd** in India.

111.s: Under the Twelfth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, existing SCCL coal linkages for AP thermal plants were:
111.x: Existing SCCL linkages were kept unchanged, and new linkages were to be provided under the Government of India's coal policy.
xa: SCCL equity: **51%** Telangana + **49%** GoI.
APGENCO units split by **location**.
AP installed capacity **16,615 MW**; renewables **8,998 MW**.

111.s: Under the arrangement relating to onshore oil and gas, royalties accrue to:
o: The State where the resource is produced
The State with the largest coastline
Both successor States in equal shares
111.x: Onshore oil and gas royalties go to the producing State, while gas allocation follows Government of India policy.
111.tq: Ask which authority or State receives the economic benefit from production.
xs: Onshore oil and gas royalties go to **the State where the resource is produced** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Gas allocation** follows **GoI policy** (Twelfth Schedule).
xa: **Mines and Minerals Amendment Act 2026** criticised for curbing States' power to tax mineral land after the **2024** **MADA vs SAIL** ruling.
Coal linkages: SCCL's existing linkages continue unchanged.

111.s:
Assertion (A): After bifurcation, Andhra Pradesh received only about 46% of Central Generating Station power though it had about 58% of the population.
Reason (R): Central Generating Station power was divided on the basis of the last five years' consumption.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
111.x: CGS power was split by the last five years' consumption, not by population, which is why AP got about 46% despite having about 58% of the population.
xa: **SCCL**'s existing coal linkages continue unchanged under the **Twelfth Schedule** of APRA.
**Srisailam** and **Nagarjuna Sagar**: left-bank power houses in Telangana, right-bank in AP.
**Singareni Collieries** equity = **51% Telangana + 49% GoI**.

111.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Green India Mission?
o: It was launched in 2011 as one of the eight missions under the NAPCC
It targets 10 million hectares of new forest cover
It is linked to an additional carbon sink of 2.5-3.0 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2030
Its sub-missions cover forest quality, forest cover and livelihoods
111.x: GIM targets 5 mha of new forest cover plus 5 mha of quality improvement, not 10 mha of new cover. The other three statements are correct.
xa: **NAP and GIM** merged from **2021-22**; run through the **SFDA** (federation of **22 FDAs**).
**Nagar Van Yojana:** **61 Nagar Vans** sanctioned to AP; State's **Nagaravanam:** **37** city forests.
National Forest Policy **1988** aims at **33%** cover (**66%** in hills).

111.s: Which one of the following is the principal function of CAMPA as described in the relevant framework?
o: It manages only urban parks in municipal areas.
It allocates coal linkages to thermal power plants.
It spends compensatory levies collected for forest land diverted to non-forest use on afforestation.
It fixes the minimum support price for all agricultural crops.
111.x: CAMPA, set up by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, uses compensatory levies for afforestation after forest land is diverted to non-forest use.
111.tq: Ask which institution would perform the compensatory-afforestation function.
xs: **CAMPA** spends **compensatory levies** for forest land diverted to **non-forest use** on **afforestation** — option **(3)**.
It was set up by the **MoEFCC**.
Coal linkages and MSP have nothing to do with CAMPA.
xa: Forest land diverted (Apr-Dec 2025): **149.5687 ha** under **FCA 1980**.
FCA 1980 renamed **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam** from **29 Dec 2023**.

111.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
o: It recognises the habitat rights of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups
It gives ownership rights over minor forest produce
Under it, the Gram Sabha recommends diversion of forest land only for commercial mining
111.x: Under FRA the Gram Sabha recommends diversion of forest land for public utilities, not commercial mining. PVTG habitat rights, MFP ownership and nistar rights are all recognised.
xa: **PESA 1996:** Gram Sabhas control **MFP**.
**Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980** renamed **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam** from **29 Dec 2023**.
**AP Forest Act 1967, Section 28:** power to declare that a protected forest ceases to be one.

111.s: As per the 2023-24 remeasurement, the coastline of Andhra Pradesh is:
111.x: The 2023-24 remeasurement gives 1,053.07 km, the third-longest after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu; 974 km is the older figure.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** some notes say "longest" — wrong.
Telangana is landlocked; AP kept the **entire coastline**.
Fisheries: AP ≈ **29%** of India's fish.

111.s: Which notified non-major port of Andhra Pradesh handles the most cargo?
111.x: Krishnapatnam handles the most cargo among the notified non-major ports; Visakhapatnam is the State's one major port.
xa: **17** notified non-major ports under **GoAP**.
⚠ Only **1** major port (Visakhapatnam); most cargo among non-major = **Krishnapatnam**.

111.s: The Red Sanders Protection Scheme covers Seshachalam, Veligonda, Lankamala, Talakona and ____ ranges.
111.x: The scheme covers the five ranges Seshachalam, Veligonda, Lankamala, Nallamala and Talakona.
xa: Districts: **Annamayya, Kadapa, Nandyal, Chittoor, Nellore, Tirupati, Prakasam**.
2023-24: **₹2,500 lakh** allocated; **₹1,529 lakh** spent.
Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve: **4,756 sq km**.

111.s: Regarding ports of Andhra Pradesh, which pair is correctly matched?
111.x: Visakhapatnam is AP's one major port; there are 17 notified non-major ports and four greenfield ports under construction.
xa: Greenfield: **Ramayapatnam** (74% done), **Mulapeta**, **Machilipatnam** and one more.
Most cargo among non-major ports: **Krishnapatnam**.
**17** includes **3** captive ports.

111.s: Andhra Pradesh is the third-largest producer of which mineral, after Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh?
111.x: Andhra Pradesh is the third-largest limestone producer after Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh. Limestone occurs in Kurnool, Kadapa, Guntur, Palnadu and NTR districts.
111.tq: Use the producer ranking to identify the mineral.
xs: AP is **3rd** in **Limestone** after **Rajasthan** and **MP** — option **(4)** is correct (LENS, Oct 2025).
Limestone districts: **Kurnool, Kadapa, Guntur, Palnadu, NTR**.
xa: Barytes: **Mangampet** — largest in India.
Bauxite: **615 MT** resources (Visakhapatnam Agency).
Uranium: **Tummalapalle**.

111.s: The beach-sand minerals ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet and monazite are associated in Andhra Pradesh mainly with the coastal areas of:
111.x: These beach-sand minerals occur mainly along the Srikakulam, Visakhapatnam and Kakinada coast.
111.tq: Group several minerals with their common geographical belt.
xs: Beach sand minerals lie on the **Srikakulam, Visakhapatnam and Kakinada** coast — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kurnool-Kadapa-Palnadu** = limestone; **Araku-Chintapalli-Paderu** = bauxite; **Tummalapalle** = uranium.
xa: Minerals: **ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet, monazite**.
AP kept coastal + basin minerals after bifurcation.

111.s: Among the old districts of Andhra Pradesh, which had the highest forest cover?
111.x: Visakhapatnam had the highest forest cover; YSR Kadapa had the largest forest area and Krishna the least.
xa: Largest forest: **Nallamala** (NSTR).
Forest type: mostly **tropical dry deciduous**.
Dry deciduous belt: **Kadapa and Kurnool** (**75-100 cm**).

111.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
111.x: The left-bank power houses of Srisailam and Nagarjuna Sagar are in Telangana, whereas the right-bank power houses are in Andhra Pradesh.
111.tq: Find the location reversal in the paired left-bank and right-bank arrangement.
xs: **Left-bank power houses — Andhra Pradesh** is NOT correct — option **(1)**: the left-bank houses are in **Telangana**.
**Right-bank** houses are in **AP**; **Srisailam** and **Nagarjuna Sagar** are shared hydro projects.
xa: Disputes arise over **hydel drawal**; **Schedule XI** puts irrigation first.
Nallamala/NSTR is also shared with Telangana.

111.s: Under Schedule XI of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, which use of water gets the highest priority?
111.x: Schedule XI gives drinking water priority over irrigation and irrigation priority over power; tribunal allocations already made remain unchanged.
xa: Undivided AP's **KWDT-I** Krishna allocation: **811 TMC**; ad hoc split **66:34** (AP **512** : TG **299** TMC).
Ongoing projects to be completed: **Handri-Neeva, Telugu Ganga, Galeru-Nagari, Veligonda**, Kalwakurthy, Nettempadu.
**Polavaram** is a **national project** under **Sec. 90**.

111.s: Polavaram is declared a national project under which section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
111.x: Polavaram is a national project under Section 90, and Telangana's consent is deemed to have been given.
xa: Only project declared national by the **Reorganisation Act itself**.
**7 Khammam mandals** moved to AP (Polavaram Ordinance).

111.s: The planned power-generation capacity of the Polavaram Project is:
111.x: Polavaram is associated with 960 MW of generation, irrigation of 7.20 lakh acres and transfer of 80 TMC to the Krishna basin.
xa: Polavaram = national project (**Sec. 90**); Telangana's consent **deemed given**.
**Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar** uses only floodwater flowing to sea (Jan 2026).
AP area rose to **1,62,970 sq km** with the Khammam mandals.

111.s: Which region of Andhra Pradesh is largely rain-shadow and drought-prone?
111.x: The Godavari, Krishna and Penna deltas are fertile coastal alluvium, while Rayalaseema is rain-shadow and drought-prone.
xa: AP has **6 agro-climatic zones**.
Rainfall (Jun-Dec 2025): **896.8 mm** = **4.2%** above normal.

111.s: The number of agro-climatic zones identified for Andhra Pradesh is:
111.x: Andhra Pradesh is divided into six agro-climatic zones in the cited data.
111.tq: Recall the exact classification count and reject nearby numerical distractors.
xs: AP has **6** agro-climatic zones — option **(3)** is correct.
The notes give **6 agro-climatic zones**, not 4, 5 or 8.
xa: Fertile deltas: **Godavari, Krishna, Penna**.
**Rayalaseema**: rain-shadow, drought-prone.
Groundwater development (2025-26): **31.5%**.

111.s: Which of the following did residual Andhra Pradesh lose after bifurcation?
111.x: AP retained the coast, the deltas and the Krishna-Godavari tail-end, but lost coal and the Hyderabad industrial base.
xa: Telangana is **landlocked** → AP kept the **entire coastline** + all ports.
AP ("**Ratna Garbha**") kept coastal + basin minerals.
Krishna: ad hoc split **66:34** (AP **512** : TG **299** TMC).

111.s: Under the 2014 ad hoc arrangement, KWDT-I's 811 TMC for undivided AP was shared between AP and Telangana as:
111.x: AP got 512 TMC and Telangana 299 TMC, about 66:34; the 58:42 population ratio was not used for Krishna water.
xa: Schedule XI: tribunal allocations **remain unchanged**.
Polavaram diverts **80 TMC** to the Krishna basin.

111.s: Which one of the following statements about forest cover is NOT correct?
o: Telangana's forest cover is reported as 26,853 sq km or 23.95 per cent.
ISFR is published annually by the Forest Survey of India from Hyderabad.
India's forest cover in ISFR 2023 was 21.76 per cent.
India's forest plus tree cover in ISFR 2023 was 25.17 per cent.
111.x: ISFR is published every two years by the Forest Survey of India, headquartered at Dehradun. The other three figures are correct.
111.tq: Use the publication frequency and institutional location as the trap in an otherwise factual set.
xs: Statement **(2)** is NOT correct: ISFR is published **every two years** by **FSI**, **Dehradun** — not annually, not from Hyderabad.
Telangana forest cover **26,853 sq km** (**23.95%**) is correct as stated.
xa: ISFR 2023 released **Dec 2024**.
Forest cover = canopy density **≥10%**.
AP forest cover (VDF+MDF+OF): **30,084.96 sq km**.

111.s: Forest and tree cover together account for what percentage of the geographical area of Andhra Pradesh?
111.x: Forest plus tree cover accounts for 21.74% of Andhra Pradesh's geographical area according to the cited APPSC assessment.
111.tq: Use the exact combined-cover figure rather than the forest-only percentage.
xs: Forest + tree cover = **21.74%** of AP's area — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC 2025 key).
**23.59%** is forest area incl. scrub; **22.96%** is notified forest area.
xa: National Forest Policy 1988 aims **33%** (**66%** in hills).
TTD: **89.40%** green cover in Tirumala, Seshachalam Hills.

111.s: As per ISFR 2021, Andhra Pradesh's Recorded Forest Area of 37,258 sq km ranked it ____ in India.
111.x: AP's Recorded Forest Area was 37,258 sq km and it ranked eighth in India, not fifth.

111.s: For ISFR classification, forest cover means land with a tree canopy density of at least:
111.x: Forest cover is land with canopy density of at least 10%, irrespective of legal ownership or notification status.
xa: ISFR published every **two years** by **FSI (Dehradun)**.
Scrub (**8,351.62 sq km**) is not counted as forest cover.

111.s: Why is the figure of 38,436.58 sq km, or 23.59%, not identical to the ISFR 2023 forest-cover figure for Andhra Pradesh?
o: It represents the geographical area of Nallamala alone.
It includes only mangrove and littoral vegetation.
It excludes moderately dense forest and open forest.
It includes 8,351.62 sq km of scrub, which ISFR does not count as forest cover.
111.x: The larger figure includes 8,351.62 sq km of scrub. ISFR’s forest-cover calculation does not count this scrub area as forest cover.
111.tq: Resolve a data discrepancy by identifying the excluded or additionally included category.
xs: It **includes 8,351.62 sq km of scrub**, which ISFR does not count as forest cover — option **(4)** is correct.
Forest cover proper (VDF+MDF+OF) is **30,084.96 sq km**.
xa: ⚠ **23.59%** (incl. scrub) vs **21.74%** (forest + tree cover).
Forest cover = canopy density **≥10%**.

111.s: Andhra Pradesh is predominantly covered by which type of forest?
111.x: AP is mostly tropical dry deciduous forest and has 3 national parks, 13 wildlife sanctuaries and 1 tiger reserve.
xa: Protected area **8,139.88 sq km**.
Mangroves ("**Coringa**") at Godavari and Krishna mouths.
Dry deciduous: **Kadapa and Kurnool**.

111.s: Which of the following provisions is associated with the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 rather than the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
o: Recognition of community or nistar rights
Ownership of minor forest produce by forest-rights holders
Control of minor forest produce by Gram Sabhas
111.x: PESA, 1996 gives Gram Sabhas control over minor forest produce. Ownership of minor forest produce, PVTG habitat rights and community or nistar rights are associated here with the FRA, 2006.
111.tq: Separate the similar-looking roles of PESA and FRA by assigning each provision to the correct law.
xs: **Control of minor forest produce by Gram Sabhas** is a **PESA 1996** provision — option **(3)**.
**FRA 2006** gives **ownership of MFP**, **nistar** rights and **PVTG habitat rights**.
xa: FRA: the Gram Sabha recommends diversion for **public utilities**.
**VSS** = village **JFM** bodies.

111.s: Andhra Pradesh accounts for approximately what share of India's cultured-shrimp exports?
111.x: AP accounts for about 75 per cent of India's cultured-shrimp exports and about 29 per cent of India's fish production.
xa: Mangroves at the river mouths are called "**Coringa** forests".
**Great Green Wall of AP**: mangroves → palmyra → wider green cover.

111.s: Which is the largest forest of Andhra Pradesh, home to NSTR, India's largest tiger reserve?
111.x: Nallamala is AP's largest forest; NSTR, India's largest tiger reserve, lies in it and is shared with Telangana.
xa: Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve: **4,756 sq km**.
Red sanders ranges include **Nallamala**, Seshachalam, Veligonda, Lankamala, Talakona.

111.s: In Andhra Pradesh, tidal or mangrove forests occur mainly at:
o: The mouths of the Godavari and Krishna
111.x: Mangrove (Coringa) forests occur near the Godavari and Krishna mouths; moist deciduous forests are in the north-coastal hills, dry deciduous in Kadapa-Kurnool and thorn-scrub in interior Rayalaseema.
xa: AP's forests are mostly **tropical dry deciduous**.
Rainfall: moist deciduous **125-200 cm**; dry deciduous **75-100 cm**; thorn/scrub **below 75 cm**.
AP has the **second-largest mangrove** ecosystem (Godavari-Krishna estuaries).

111.s: How many Nagar Vans were sanctioned to Andhra Pradesh under the Central Nagar Van Yojana?
111.x: The Central Nagar Van Yojana sanctioned 61 Nagar Vans; the State's Nagaravanam programme completed 37 city forests and seven Temple Eco-parks.
xa: ⚠ Do not mix up **Nagaravanam (37)** and **NVY (61)**.
NVY: sanctioned between **2021-22 and 2024-25**; **₹9,913.926 lakh** released, **₹5,248.641 lakh** spent by **31 Dec 2024**.
⚠ The 2023 PYQ on the NVY count has no answer key.

111.s: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 was renamed as the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 with effect from:
111.x: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 was renamed with effect from 29 December 2023. The change was an amendment and not a repeal of the law.
111.tq: Use the exact effective date and distinguish renaming by amendment from repeal.
xs: The FCA 1980 became the **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980** from **29 December 2023** — option **(2)**.
It was **amended, not repealed**.
xa: Forest land diverted (Apr-Dec 2025): **149.5687 ha** under FCA 1980.
**CAMPA** spends compensatory levies on afforestation.
**FRA 2006**: Gram Sabha recommends diversion for **public utilities**.

111.s: Under Section 28 of the Andhra Pradesh Forest Act, 1967, which power is conferred?
o: Power to declare that a protected forest ceases to be a protected forest
Power to determine the minimum support price of minor forest produce
Power to authorise diversion of any forest land for mining
Power to declare that a reserved forest has become a village forest
111.x: Section 28 confers the power to declare that a protected forest ceases to be a protected forest.
111.tq: Match the exact statutory section with the specific power rather than a neighbouring forest-law function.
xs: Section 28 gives the **power to declare that a protected forest ceases to be a protected forest** — option **(1)** (APPSC **2024**).
This is under the **AP Forest Act 1967**.
xa: **FCA 1980** renamed **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam** from **29 Dec 2023**.
**PESA 1996**: Gram Sabhas control **MFP**.
AP ranks **8th** in **Recorded Forest Area**.

111.s: The National Forest Policy that preceded PESA (1996) and the Forest Rights Act (2006) was issued in:
111.x: The National Forest Policy was issued in 1988, followed by PESA in 1996, FRA in 2006 and APRA in 2014.
xa: **FCA 1980** predates all four; renamed from **29 Dec 2023**.
**Green India Mission**: **2011**.

111.s: The National Forest Policy, 1988 envisages what forest cover for hilly areas?
111.x: The 1988 policy aims at 33% overall forest cover and 66% in the hills; AP has about 23.6% forest cover.
xa: ISFR 2023: AP forest area incl. scrub **38,436.58 sq km** = **23.59%**.
⚠ Forest + tree cover = **21.74%** (APPSC 2025 key).

111.s: For what reason did the Andhra Pradesh government protest Telangana’s use of the Srisailam reservoir water in June 2021?
o: Telangana is generating power below 834 feet
Telangana is generating power above 834 feet
Telangana is generating power above 1200 feet
Telangana is generating power above 1000 feet

111.s: As per India State Forest report, Andhra Pradesh is also ranked ______ in terms of the Recorded Forest Area (RFA).
As per India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2019, what is the rank of Andhra Pradesh State in terms of the Recorded Forest Area (RFA) which is 37,258 sq km?

112.s: The Hyderabad region, including Rangareddy and Medak, contributed nearly what share of the undivided State's tax and non-tax revenue?
112.x: The Hyderabad region, together with Rangareddy and Medak, contributed nearly 50 percent of the undivided State's tax and non-tax revenue.
112.tq: Use the region-based share rather than the city-specific figure.
xs: The **Hyderabad region** (+ **Rangareddy, Medak**) gave **nearly 50 percent** of undivided AP's tax + non-tax revenue — option **(3)**.
Key sources: **corporate taxes**, **stamp duties**, **commercial taxes**.
xa: Losing Hyderabad left AP with a **structural revenue deficit**.
Lost assets: **HITEC City**, Financial District, **Genome Valley**, corporate and bank head offices.
Tax impact: lower **GST (then VAT)**, stamp duty and **motor-vehicle tax** collections.

112.s: Which one of the following was NOT identified as part of the economic base lost with Hyderabad?
o: The entire agricultural base of residual Andhra Pradesh
HITEC City and the Financial District
112.x: The lost economic base included HITEC City, the Financial District, Genome Valley, corporate and bank head offices, commercial real estate and related MSME supply chains. It did not comprise the entire agricultural base of residual Andhra Pradesh.
112.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the Hyderabad economic cluster.
xs: **The entire agricultural base of residual AP** was NOT lost with Hyderabad — option **(1)**.
Lost: **HITEC City + Financial District**, **Genome Valley** pharma cluster, **corporate and bank head offices**, commercial real estate, MSME supply chains.
xa: Effect: **structural revenue deficit** and a **narrower tax base**.
Tax collections cut: **GST (then VAT)**, stamp duty, motor-vehicle tax.

112.s: In January 2026, the amount of special assistance fast-tracked for Amaravati was
112.x: Special assistance of ₹15,000 crore was fast-tracked for Amaravati in January 2026.
112.tq: Use the distinctive figure and date to distinguish the Amaravati assistance from the broader assistance package.
xs: **₹15,000 crore** central assistance was **fast-tracked for Amaravati** — option **(2)**.
**₹3,979 crore** was the 2014-15 RD grant.
xa: Sec. 94(3): **₹2,500 crore** for **capital buildings**.
AP blames the **loss of capital city** among its fiscal pressures.

112.s: The resource-gap estimates for Andhra Pradesh were ₹4,118 crore, ₹13,776 crore and ₹16,078 crore according to, respectively:
o: The Union Finance Ministry, the CAG and the State
The Union Finance Ministry, the State and the CAG
The State, the Union Finance Ministry and the CAG
The CAG, the State and the Union Finance Ministry
112.x: The Union estimate was ₹4,118 crore, the CAG-linked estimate was ₹13,776 crore and the State estimate was ₹16,078 crore.
112.tq: Match each figure with the authority that produced or reported it.
xs: **₹4,118 crore** = **Union Finance Ministry**; **₹13,776 crore** = **CAG**; **₹16,078 crore** = **State** — option **(1)**.
The CAG figure covers **2 Jun 2014 - 31 Mar 2015** (APPSC-GS 2016 key).
xa: Centre's lower figure excluded scheme costs like the **farm-loan waiver**.
⚠ The printed APPSC 2016 key is garbled ("...3,776 Cr"); it is not ₹20,745 / 16,211 / 21,481 crore.
APPSC-GS 2022 key: gap **more than ₹15,000 crore**.

112.s: The resource gap of Andhra Pradesh in the bifurcation year (2014-15) was:
o: Between Rs 5,000 crore and Rs 10,000 crore
Between Rs 10,000 crore and Rs 12,000 crore
112.x: The APPSC-GS 2022 key puts the bifurcation-year gap at more than Rs 15,000 crore (the State itself claimed Rs 16,078 crore). The lower ranges match only the Union Finance Ministry's narrower assessment of about Rs 4,118 crore or are unsupported.
xs: APPSC-GS 2022 key: the bifurcation-year gap was **more than Rs 15,000 crore** — option **(4)**.
AP's own claim was **₹16,078 crore**.
The lower ranges fit only the Centre's narrower ≈ **₹4,118 crore**.
xa: CAG figure: **₹13,776 crore** (2 Jun 2014 - 31 Mar 2015).
Resource gap = **revenue deficit** for the first ten months.
112.fixed: drop 'according to APPSC answer key' wording; no exam phrases it so

112.s: As per the APPSC 2021 reference, the revenue deficit of Andhra Pradesh for 2022-23 was projected at about:
112.x: The 2022-23 revenue deficit was projected at about Rs 17,000 crore; the actual turned out to be Rs 43,487 crore (3.3% of GSDP). Rs 4,118 crore was the Union's 2014-15 gap estimate and Rs 60,285 crore is the 2024-25 revenue deficit.
xs: The 2022-23 RD was projected at about **Rs 17,000 crore** (APPSC **2021**) — option **(2)**.
The actual was **₹43,487 crore** (**3.3%**).
**₹4,118 crore** was the Centre's 2014-15 gap estimate; **₹60,285 crore** is the 2024-25 RD.
xa: CAG flagged high revenue deficit **three years running**.

112.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the appointed day for the bifurcation of the State was:
112.x: The State was divided on 2 June 2014, which was the appointed day. The Act received presidential assent on 1 March 2014.
112.tq: Distinguish the date of assent from the appointed day.
xs: The **appointed day** was **2 June 2014** — option **(2)**.
⚠ The Act got assent on **1 March 2014**; "came into effect on **2 March 2014**" is a wrong claim in some notes.
**31 March 2015** ends the **first year** (2 June 2014 - 31 March 2015).
xa: **Resource gap** = revenue deficit for the **first ten months**.
CAG put the 2014-15 revenue deficit at **₹13,776 crore**.

112.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the difference between the Centre’s and Andhra Pradesh’s estimates of the post-bifurcation resource gap?
o: The Centre calculated only capital expenditure, whereas the State calculated only tax expenditure
The Centre used CAG figures, whereas the State used Finance Commission projections
The Centre included all new State schemes, whereas the State excluded them
The Centre used standardised accounting and excluded new State schemes, whereas the State counted its actual expenditure
112.x: The Union calculation used standardised accounting and left out new State schemes, while Andhra Pradesh counted its actual spending.
112.tq: Split the options by comparing the accounting method and treatment of new schemes.
xs: The **Centre used standardised accounting and excluded new State schemes**; the **State counted its actual expenditure** — option **(4)**.
Option (3) reverses the positions.
xa: Centre's figure ≈ **₹4,118 crore**; State's **₹16,078 crore**; CAG **₹13,776 crore**.
First year: **2 June 2014** to **31 March 2015**.

112.s: In the context of Andhra Pradesh's bifurcation, the 'resource gap' for the first post-bifurcation year refers to:
o: The fiscal deficit of the State for the full financial year 2014-15
The revenue deficit (revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts) for the first ten months
The shortfall in capital outlay compared with the 13th Finance Commission projection
The difference between borrowings and repayments for 2014-15
112.x: The resource gap was defined as the revenue deficit, i.e. revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts, for the first ten months (2 June 2014 to 31 March 2015). It is not the full-year fiscal deficit, a capital-outlay shortfall or a net borrowing figure.
112.tq: Resource gap = revenue deficit, first 10 months.
xs: Resource gap = **the revenue deficit (revenue expenditure − revenue receipts) for the first ten months** — option **(2)**.
Period: **2 June 2014** (appointed day) to **31 March 2015**.
It is not the full-year **fiscal deficit**, a capital-outlay shortfall or net borrowing.
xa: Estimates: CAG **₹13,776 crore**; State **₹16,078 crore**; Centre ≈ **₹4,118 crore**.
RD grant for 2014-15: **₹3,979 crore**.

112.s: The Fourteenth Finance Commission fixed a normative post-devolution revenue gap for Andhra Pradesh from:
112.x: The 14th FC fixed a normative, static post-devolution gap from 2015-16; AP argued its actual deficits exceeded it.
xa: 14th FC gave AP **₹22,113 crore** post-devolution RD grants over **2015-20**.
14th FC raised devolution from **32% to 42%**.

112.s: Andhra Pradesh sought tax holidays for post-bifurcation industrialisation under which section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
112.x: AP's demands included tax holidays under Section 94(1) and backward-area packages under Section 46, besides revenue-deficit grants, Polavaram funding and capital-city grants.
xa: Main demand: **Special Category Status**.

112.s: The Special Assistance Measure for Andhra Pradesh involved the Centre funding what share of externally aided projects?
112.x: Under the Special Assistance Measure, the Centre funded the 90 percent share of externally aided projects, serving as an alternative to Special Category Status.
112.tq: Distinguish the project-support share from general tax devolution percentages.
xs: Under **SAM**, the Centre funds **90 percent** of **externally aided projects** — option **(4)**.
It was given **instead of SCS**.
**32%** and **42%** are devolution shares; **60%** is the normal CSS share.
xa: ⚠ SCS meant **90%** of **CSS costs**; SAM = **90%** of **externally aided projects**.
The **₹3,979 crore** RD grant was part of SAM.

112.s:
Assertion (A): Under Special Category Status, the Centre would bear 90 percent of Centrally Sponsored Scheme costs.
Reason (R): Under the ordinary arrangement, the Centre bears only 60 percent of such costs.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
112.x: Both are true: SCS gives a 90 percent central share and 60 percent is the ordinary arrangement. R is only a contrast and does not explain A.
xa: ⚠ **SAM** = Centre funds **90%** of **externally aided projects** instead of SCS.
Centre refused citing the **14th FC**.

112.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
A. Enactment of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act
B. 14th Finance Commission raises States' share of the divisible pool from 32% to 42%
C. TDP leaves the NDA over the Special Category Status row
112.x: APRA was enacted in 2014, the 14th FC award (raising devolution to 42%) applied from 2015, and the TDP left the NDA in 2018.
xa: Under SCS the Centre bears **90%** of CSS costs (vs **60%**).
Instead, the **Special Assistance Measure (SAM)** — Centre funds **90%** of **externally aided projects**.

112.s: How much central assistance was provided for capital buildings of Andhra Pradesh under Section 94(3) of the Reorganisation Act?
112.x: ₹2,500 crore was given for capital buildings under Section 94(3); ₹3,979 crore was the 2014-15 revenue deficit grant and ₹22,113 crore the 2015-20 post-devolution grants.
xa: **₹15,000 crore** central assistance fast-tracked for **Amaravati**.

112.s: Under the 16th Finance Commission, which ended revenue deficit grants for all States, Andhra Pradesh's share of the divisible pool rose to:
112.x: The 16th FC ended revenue deficit grants for all States, and AP's divisible-pool share rose to 4.22%.
xa: **14th FC** gave AP **₹22,113 crore** in RD grants (**2015-20**).
14th FC devolution: **32% → 42%**.

112.s: In February 2021, Andhra Pradesh became the ______ State to undertake the power-sector reforms stipulated by the Department of Expenditure.
112.x: The stated APPSC 2023 answer key treated Andhra Pradesh as the second State to undertake the reforms.
112.tq: Test the ordinal detail directly, since close ordinal distractors are commonly used.
xs: AP was the **second** State to undertake the DoE power reforms (**February 2021**) — option **(3)** (APPSC **2023** key).
The reforms unlocked the extra **0.5%** borrowing over **3.5%** of GSDP.
xa: CAG: power subsidy at **121%** (2023) and **120%** (2024) of BE.
**APSPDCL**: first AP DISCOM to connect **50,000** rooftop-solar services.

112.s: Corporate taxes, stamp duties and ____ were important components of the Hyderabad region's revenue in the undivided State.
112.x: Corporate taxes, stamp duties and commercial taxes were key parts of Hyderabad's revenue contribution; agricultural land revenue was not its basis.
xa: Hyderabad region gave nearly **50%** of undivided AP's tax + non-tax revenue.
Loss of HITEC City + Financial District → loss of **IT/ITeS exports**.
Result: a **narrower tax base** for residual AP.

112.s: In the 2026-27 Budget Estimates of Andhra Pradesh, the revenue deficit and fiscal deficit are respectively about:
112.x: 2026-27 BE: RD Rs 22,002 crore (1.11%) and FD Rs 75,868 crore (3.84%). 3.79%/5.11% are 2024-25 Finance Accounts, 2.33%/4.57% are 2025-26 RE, and 3.3%/4.3% mix the 2022-23 RD and 2023-24 FD ratios.
xs: In rupees: RD **₹22,002 crore**, FD **₹75,868 crore**.
xa: Rounded Budget 2026-27 targets: RD **1.1%**, FD **3.8%**.

112.s: In FY25, the combined fiscal deficit of Indian States stood at about:
112.x: States' combined fiscal deficit was about 3.2% of GDP in FY25, and revenue balances worsened in 18 States between FY19 and FY25.
xa: ⚠ The notes' national context says only that **18 states'** revenue balances worsened FY19-FY25.

112.s: The debt of Andhra Pradesh in the 2024-25 revised estimates was reported as ₹5,64,488 crore, equivalent to
112.x: Andhra Pradesh's debt was reported at ₹5,64,488 crore, or 35.15 percent of GSDP, in the 2024-25 revised estimates.
112.tq: Match the absolute debt figure with its corresponding ratio rather than confusing it with deficit ratios.
xs: Debt of **₹5,64,488 crore** = **35.15 percent of GSDP** (2024-25 RE) — option **(1)**.
Market loans make up **75%** of it.

112.s: As per Accounts at a Glance 2024-25, Andhra Pradesh's fiscal deficit, against an FRBM ceiling of 4%, was:
112.x: AP recorded a fiscal deficit of 5.05% against the 4% ceiling and a revenue deficit of 3.75% against the 2.70% target.
xa: Finance Accounts give **3.79% / 5.11%**.
Borrowings **₹81,071 crore**; misstatements ~**₹6,120 crore**.

112.s: The additional borrowing window linked to power-sector reforms permitted States to borrow up to:
o: 3.5% of GSDP, with an additional 0.5% conditional on power-sector reforms
4% of GSDP, with an additional 1% conditional on tax reforms
112.x: The Department of Expenditure allowed a fiscal deficit of 3.5% of GSDP plus an additional 0.5% if power-sector reforms were undertaken.
112.tq: Separate the basic borrowing limit from the conditional additional window.
xs: Borrowing window: FD **3.5% of GSDP + 0.5%** conditional on **power-sector reforms** — option **(1)**.
It was set by the **Department of Expenditure**.
xa: AP undertook the DoE reforms in **February 2021** — the **second** State.
CAG: power subsidy spending at **121% (2023)** and **120% (2024)** of BE.

112.s: In March 2023, Andhra Pradesh’s off-budget borrowings were equivalent to approximately
112.x: The CAG assessed the ₹1.28 lakh crore off-budget borrowing burden in March 2023 at 9.7% of GSDP.
112.tq: Use the percentage associated with the specified year, not a later guarantee ratio.
xs: Off-budget borrowings of **₹1.28 lakh crore** = **9.7% of GSDP** (March 2023, CAG) — option **(1)**.
They rose from **₹1,18,394 crore** in **Mar 2022**.
xa: Market loans = **75%** of debt.

112.s: In response to the revenue loss caused by bifurcation, the then Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu primarily demanded:
o: Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh
A uniform tax holiday for all States
Transfer of Hyderabad to residual Andhra Pradesh
112.x: N. Chandrababu Naidu demanded Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh, citing the State's post-bifurcation revenue difficulties.
112.tq: Identify the principal political demand associated with the revenue-loss issue.
xs: CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu** demanded **Special Category Status (SCS)** — option **(1)** (APPSC-GS 2018 key).
SCS for **5 years** had been promised on the floor of the **Rajya Sabha** in **2014**.
xa: Under SCS the Centre bears **90%** of CSS costs (vs **60%**) + tax breaks.
The Centre cited the **14th FC** to refuse SCS.
The SCS row → **TDP left NDA** in **2018**.

112.s: Among the central institutions given to residual Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation, which pair is correctly matched?
112.x: The institutions are IIT Tirupati, IIM Visakhapatnam, NIT Tadepalligudem and AIIMS Mangalagiri. So NIT - Tadepalligudem is correct; IIT and IIM locations are swapped in the first two options, and AIIMS is at Mangalagiri.
112.tq: IIT Tirupati, IIM Vizag, NIT Tadepalligudem, AIIMS Mangalagiri.
xs: **NIT - Tadepalligudem** is correctly matched — option **(3)**.
**IIT** is at **Tirupati**, **IIM** at **Visakhapatnam**, **AIIMS** at **Mangalagiri**.
xa: AP got **11** central institutions.
Sec. **94(3)**: **₹2,500 crore** for capital buildings.

112.s: In 2022-23, the state of Andhra Pradesh is expected to have a revenue deficit of approximately how many crores?
Andhra Pradesh has become the Ministry of Finance in February 2021. State to undertake the power sector reforms stipulated by the Department of Expenditure,
