112.s: In February 2021, Andhra Pradesh became the ________ State to undertake the power sector reforms stipulated by the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance.

113.s: Justice R.S. Bachawat was the Chairperson of which pair of tribunals?
113.x: Justice R.S. Bachawat chaired KWDT-I and the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal, whereas KWDT-II was chaired by Justice Brijesh Kumar.
113.tq: Discriminate between tribunal chairpersons by matching the repeated name with the correct two tribunals.
xs: Justice **R.S. Bachawat** chaired **KWDT-I and GWDT** — option **(4)**.
**KWDT-II** was chaired by Justice **Brijesh Kumar**, so options (1) and (3) are wrong.
The **Tungabhadra Board** is a board under the **Andhra State Act, 1953**, not a tribunal.
xa: KWDT-I award **1973**, final **1976**; GWDT award **1980**.
KWDT-II award **2010** (further report **2013**).
GWDT was based on **inter-State agreements**.

113.s: At 75 per cent dependability, which set of shares was awarded by KWDT-I to Maharashtra, Karnataka and the united Andhra Pradesh respectively?
113.x: KWDT-I awarded 560 TMC to Maharashtra, 700 TMC to Karnataka and 800 TMC to the united Andhra Pradesh at 75 per cent dependability.
113.tq: Use the fixed three-State numerical sequence and avoid swapping neighbouring entries.
xs: **560, 700 and 800 TMC** — Maharashtra, Karnataka, united AP — option **(2)**.
These are KWDT-I shares at **75%** dependability.
xa: AP's **800** + **11** return flows = **811 TMC** (APPSC-GS 2021 key gives AP **800**).

113.s: The united Andhra Pradesh share of 800 TMC under KWDT-I became 811 TMC when what was added?
113.x: The 800 TMC allocation, together with 11 TMC of return flows, produced the 811 TMC figure used in the ad hoc division.
113.tq: Test the small numerical component that explains the difference between two closely related totals.
xs: **11 TMC of return flows** were added to AP's **800 TMC** to make **811** — option **(1)**.
The notes mention no evaporation, recharge or inter-basin item in this sum.
xa: Telangana demands **50:50**, citing larger basin area.

113.s: The Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal-II was chaired by:
113.x: KWDT-II was chaired by Justice Brijesh Kumar; its award came in 2010 with a further report in 2013.
xa: CDI notes put AP's added share at **196 TMC**.

113.s: Telangana's demand for a 50:50 split of Krishna water rests on its:
113.x: Telangana's 50:50 demand rests on its larger basin area, not population; the 2014 ad hoc split gave AP 512 TMC and Telangana 299 TMC (66:34).
xa: **KWDT-I** gave **united AP 800 TMC** (+ **11** return flows).
**Sec. 89:** KWDT-II's term was extended for **project-wise allocation** and an **operational protocol** for **deficit flows**.
**KRMB** HQ is in **Andhra Pradesh**; **GRMB** HQ is in **Telangana**.

113.s: In the Cauvery water dispute, the Supreme Court’s 2018 verdict fixed the share of Tamil Nadu at:
113.x: The 2018 Cauvery verdict fixed Tamil Nadu’s share at 404.25 TMC. Karnataka, Kerala and Puducherry were allocated 284.75, 30 and 7 TMC respectively.
113.tq: Separate the largest State share from the other three figures in the comparative allocation.
xs: The SC **2018** Cauvery verdict gave **Tamil Nadu 404.25 TMC** — option **(3)**.
**Karnataka 284.75**, **Kerala 30**, **Puducherry 7** tmcft.
xa: Compare Krishna: KWDT-I gave united AP **800 TMC** (**811** with return flows).
AP's ad hoc Krishna share: **512 TMC** (**66 : 34**).

113.s:
Consider the following statements about the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal (GWDT) award of 1980:
1. According to Andhra Pradesh, the Godavari surplus has already been quantified and divided under the award.
2. It was based on inter-State agreements.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: Statement 2 is correct: the GWDT award (1980) rests on inter-State agreements. Statement 1 is wrong: AP's position is that the Godavari surplus is NOT yet quantified under the award. Hence '2 only'.
113.tq: KWDT = allocations by dependability; GWDT = agreements, surplus unquantified.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — option **(1)**.
2: correct — the **GWDT** award (**1980**) is **based on inter-State agreements**.
1: incorrect — AP says the **Godavari surplus is not yet quantified** under the award.
xa: **GWDT** was chaired by Justice **R.S. Bachawat**, who also chaired **KWDT-I**.
**KWDT-II** (Justice **Brijesh Kumar**) gave its award in **2010**; it is not notified and is challenged in the SC.
⚠ **811** TMC = **800** + **11** return flows; KWDT-I at **75%** dependability vs KWDT-II at **65%**.

113.s: Who is the Chairperson of the Apex Council constituted under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
113.x: The three-member Apex Council is chaired by the Union Minister of Water Resources, with the CMs of AP and Telangana as members.
xa: ⚠ NOT the **PM**, Home Minister or Governors.
It supervises **GRMB and KRMB**.

113.s: Under Schedule XI of the AP Reorganisation Act, a function of the KRMB and GRMB is:
o: Approving new projects on the Krishna and Godavari
Regulating supply from notified headworks according to tribunal awards
Redetermining the shares of AP and Telangana every water year
Referring water disputes to a tribunal
113.x: The Boards regulate supply from notified headworks as per tribunal awards and release water by State shares; approving projects and referring disputes belong to the Apex Council, and redetermining shares is not their function.
xa: **Sec. 88**: a Board may make regulations.
**Aug 2026**: KRMB committee allowed only **drinking water** from Srisailam + Nagarjuna Sagar.

113.s: The Tungabhadra Board was set up under Section 66 of which Act?
113.x: The Board was set up under Section 66 of the Andhra State Act, 1953; under Section 91(1) of APRA, AP and Telangana replaced undivided AP on it.
xa: **Sec. 92 / Schedule XI:** a defaulting State faces financial and other penalties.
**Sec. 88:** a Board may make regulations.

113.s:
Assertion (A): The Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards are autonomous bodies under the administrative control of the Centre.
Reason (R): Each Board has a full-time Member Secretary and one central expert.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
113.x: Under Sections 85(3) and 85(4), the Boards are autonomous bodies under Central control, each with a Central Chairperson, two members per State, a central expert and a full-time Member Secretary. R describes their composition, not why they are under Central control.
xa: **Sec. 86**: staff on deputation from both States equally; States fund the Boards.

113.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the purposes for which KWDT’s term was extended under Section 89?
o: Addressing project-wise and operational issues within the scope of the reference
Automatically dividing the undivided Andhra Pradesh share between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
Fixing an operational protocol for releases during deficit flows
Making project-wise allocations where no tribunal had done so
113.x: Section 89 covered project-wise allocation where necessary and an operational protocol for deficit flows. It did not itself automatically divide the Andhra Pradesh share between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
113.tq: Distinguish the express terms of a statutory reference from a later political or legal demand.
xs: **Automatically dividing the undivided AP share** is NOT a **Sec. 89** purpose — option **(2)**.
Sec. 89 extended KWDT-II's term for **(a) project-wise allocation** where no tribunal had done so and **(b) an operational protocol** for releases in **deficit flows**.
The division of AP's share came later through **Sec. 5(1)** of the **ISRWD Act** (**Oct 2023**).
xa: AP wanted allocations redone among **four States**.
KWDT-II award: **2010**; not notified, challenged in SC.

113.s: In October 2023, the Centre gave KWDT-II further terms of reference under:
o: Section 89 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014
Section 5(1) of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956
Section 87 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014
Section 3 of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956
113.x: The October 2023 terms of reference were given under Section 5(1) of the ISRWD Act, 1956, not Section 89 of APRA alone.
xa: **Sec. 89** extended KWDT-II's term for **project-wise allocation** and a **deficit-flow protocol**.
The **Apex Council** refers disputes not covered by KWDT to a tribunal under the **ISRWD Act, 1956**.
Apex Council: **Union Minister of Water Resources** (chair) + **CMs of AP and Telangana** — **3 members**.

113.s: Under Section 84(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Apex Council for the Krishna and Godavari rivers was constituted by the Centre from which date?
o: The date of constitution of the two River Management Boards
The date of publication of the tribunal awards
The date of enactment of the Act
113.x: Section 84(1) provides for constitution of the Apex Council by the Centre from the appointed day.
113.tq: Recall the statutory trigger date rather than the date of a later institutional action.
xs: Under **Sec. 84(1)**, the Apex Council is constituted by the Centre **from the appointed day** — option **(1)**.
The Boards came later — within **60 days** of the appointed day (**Sec. 85(1)**).
xa: **Sec. 84(3)** lists Apex Council functions.
Members: Union Minister of Water Resources (Chair) + CMs of AP and Telangana.

113.s: The power to approve a new project on the Krishna or Godavari, after appraisal by the concerned Board and the Central Water Commission, belongs to which body?
o: The Krishna River Management Board alone
The Godavari River Management Board alone
113.x: Under Section 84(3), approval of new Krishna or Godavari projects after the prescribed appraisal is a function of the Apex Council.
113.tq: Use the authority-based trap by distinguishing the Apex Council from the subordinate Boards.
xs: The **Apex Council** approves new Krishna/Godavari projects after **Board + CWC** appraisal — option **(2)**.
The **Boards** regulate supply per tribunal awards but do not sanction projects.

113.s: The Ministry of Jal Shakti notified the jurisdiction of the KRMB and GRMB on:

113.s: A State fails to comply with the directions applicable to a River Management Board. Under Section 92 read with Schedule XI, which consequence may follow?
o: Financial and other penalties imposed by the Centre
Automatic dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly
Cancellation of the relevant tribunal award by the Board
Transfer of all State water projects to the Supreme Court
113.x: A defaulting State may face financial and other penalties from the Centre under Section 92 and Schedule XI.
113.tq: Identify the consequence linked to non-compliance without confusing it with judicial or constitutional sanctions.
xs: A defaulting State faces **financial and other penalties** from the **Centre** — option **(1)** (**Sec. 92 / Schedule XI**).
Boards cannot cancel tribunal awards.

**CISF** guards reservoirs (**85(7)**).

113.s: Polavaram was declared a national project under which section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?

**Telangana and Odisha** object to Polavaram **submergence**.

113.s: Andhra Pradesh plans to divert how much Polavaram flood water through the Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar Link?
113.x: Andhra Pradesh plans to divert 200 TMC of Polavaram flood water through the proposed link.
113.tq: Distinguish the proposed diversion quantity from project-capacity and tribunal-share figures.
xs: AP plans to divert **200 TMC** of Polavaram floodwater — option **(3)**.
It would serve ~**80 lakh** people and ~**7.5 lakh** acres via reservoirs at **Bollapalli** and **Banakacherla**.
**960** is Polavaram's MW; **404.25** is TN's Cauvery share; **120 MW** is a wrong Polavaram figure.
xa: **Telangana withdrew** its SC petition against the link (Jan 2026).
AP says the link uses only floodwater flowing to the sea.

113.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the Apex Council under Section 84(3) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Referring disputes not covered by KWDT to a tribunal under the ISRWD Act, 1956
Allocating or redetermining the shares of the States in river waters
Approving new projects on the Krishna and Godavari after appraisal by the Board and the CWC
Supervising the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards
113.x: The Apex Council can supervise the Boards, approve new projects after appraisal, settle disputes by negotiation and refer certain disputes to a tribunal. Allocation or redetermination of shares is not stated as its function here.
113.tq: Separate the power to approve projects and settle disputes from the power to allocate water shares.
xs: **Allocating or redetermining the shares** is NOT an Apex Council function — option **(2)**.

Its **Sec. 84(3)** functions: **supervise both Boards**, **approve new projects** after Board + CWC appraisal, settle disputes by negotiation, refer disputes to a tribunal under the **ISRWD Act, 1956**.
xa: ⚠ Allocating shares is **not a Board function** either.
Shares come from tribunals: **KWDT-I**, **KWDT-II**, **GWDT**.

113.s: The Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar Link envisages diversion of water:
o: From the Krishna through the Godavari to the Penna
From the Godavari through the Krishna to the Penna
From the Penna through the Krishna to the Godavari
From the Godavari through the Penna to the Krishna
113.x: The link envisages diversion from the Godavari through the Krishna basin to the Penna basin.
xa: The link was earlier **Polavaram-Banakacherla**.
**Palamuru-Rangareddy**, Dindi — Telangana projects on the **Krishna**.

113.s: Telangana objects to AP's Pothireddypadu Head Regulator/Rayalaseema Lift project on the ground that Srisailam is mainly a:
113.x: Telangana's objection is that Srisailam is mainly a power project; AP built the scheme on the Krishna.

113.s: Kaleshwaram, a subject of inter-State objections, is a Telangana project on which river?
113.x: Kaleshwaram is Telangana's Godavari project; AP sought clearances for it while Telangana wants national-project status.

Telangana raised Kaleshwaram's national status at the **31st Southern Zonal Council** (Aug 2026).

113.s: Under Section 85(2) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the headquarters of the river management boards are located as follows:
o: KRMB in Telangana and GRMB in Andhra Pradesh
Both KRMB and GRMB in New Delhi
KRMB in Andhra Pradesh and GRMB in Telangana
Both KRMB and GRMB in Andhra Pradesh
113.x: Sec. 85(2) places the KRMB headquarters in Andhra Pradesh and the GRMB headquarters in Telangana. The reversed pairing is the common trap; neither New Delhi nor a single State hosts both.
113.tq: Krishna Board in AP, Godavari Board in TG.
xs: **Sec. 85(2)**: **KRMB in Andhra Pradesh**, **GRMB in Telangana** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Option (1) is the common reversed trap; neither New Delhi nor one State hosts both.
xa: Boards set up within **60 days** of the appointed day (**Sec. 85(1)**).
Jurisdiction notified **15 July 2021**.

Apex Council of Godavari and Krishna river water resources and their management consists of
o: Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana as Co-chairpersons.

Governor of Andhra Pradesh as chairperson

114.s:
Assertion (A): The Polavaram Project is designed to irrigate 7.20 lakh acres.
Reason (R): The gross reservoir capacity of Polavaram is 194.6 TMC.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
114.x: Both are true: Polavaram irrigates 7.20 lakh acres (2.91 lakh ha) and has 194.6 TMC gross capacity, but reservoir size alone does not explain the irrigation design.
xa: Hydel component: **960 MW** (**12 x 80 MW**).
Drinking/industry: **23.44 TMC** for **Visakhapatnam**; serves **28.5 lakh** people in **540 villages**.
⚠ A Jan 2026 CA note gives **120 MW** + **3.6 lakh acres** — wrong; follow the **Economic Survey**.
Dam: **2,467.50 m** earth-cum-rock fill; spillway **1,121.20 m**.

114.s: What is the installed hydel capacity of the Polavaram Project?
114.x: The Polavaram hydel component has an installed capacity of 960 MW, made up of 12 units of 80 MW each.
xa: Irrigation: **7.20 lakh acres** (= **2.91 lakh ha**).
Gross storage **194.6 TMC**; utilisation **322.73 TMC**.
**23.44 TMC** is earmarked for **Visakhapatnam** drinking water and industry.

114.s: How much Godavari water does the Polavaram Right Main Canal transfer to the Krishna?
114.x: Polavaram transfers 80 TMC of Godavari water to the Krishna through the Right Main Canal; 23.44 TMC is provided for Visakhapatnam.
xa: Split of the 80 TMC: **45 TMC** to AP + **35 TMC** to Karnataka (**21**) and Maharashtra (**14**).
**Pattiseema** is a temporary lift into the Polavaram **RMC**.
GWDT was set up in **1969**; award in **1980**.

114.s: The Polavaram Project site, earlier identified with West Godavari district, now lies in which district?
114.x: The project is near Polavaram village in Eluru district; the site was earlier identified with West Godavari district.
xa: ⚠ **West Godavari** is the old PYQ key for the district.
Dam: **2,467.50 m** earth-cum-rock fill; spillway **1,121.20 m**.
Started under **Jalayagnam** in **2005**; first contemplated in **1941**.

114.s: The Polavaram proposal was named "Ramapada Sagaram" by:
114.x: Sir Sonti Venkataramamurthy named the proposal Ramapada Sagaram; the project was first contemplated in 1941.
xa: **2014** is the year of the **AP Reorganisation Act**, whose **Section 90** made Polavaram a national project.
The **Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal** (set up **1969**) gave its award in **1980**.
Site: on the **Godavari**, near Polavaram village, **Eluru district**.

114.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal?
o: Of the 80 TMC diverted into the Krishna above Vijayawada, AP gets 45 TMC
It was set up in 1969 and gave its award in 1980
Its award cleared Polavaram with an FRL of +150 ft
Of the remaining 35 TMC, Karnataka gets 14 TMC and Maharashtra 21 TMC
114.x: The remaining 35 TMC is split 21 TMC to Karnataka and 14 TMC to Maharashtra, not the reverse.
xa: The transfer runs via the **Right Main Canal**.
Telangana says the proposed **Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar** link violates the **1980 GWDT award** and **APRA 2014**.

114.s: The proposed Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar link was earlier known as the:
114.x: The Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar link was earlier called the Banakacherla link; Telangana contends it violates APRA 2014 and the 1980 GWDT award.
xa: GWDT award: **80 TMC** Godavari water diverted into Krishna — **45** to AP, **35** to Karnataka and Maharashtra.
Polavaram: **960 MW**; **7.20 lakh acres**; FRL **45.72 m**.
The **Right Main Canal** feeds the **Krishna delta**; the **Left Main Canal** runs to **Visakhapatnam**.

114.s: The target for completion of the Polavaram Project was shifted from December 2027 to:
114.x: The completion target was moved forward from December 2027 to March 2027, before the 2027 Godavari Pushkaralu.
114.tq: Distinguish the revised target from the original target and the R&R deadline.
xs: The completion target moved from Dec 2027 to **March 2027** — option **(1)**.
The aim is to finish before the **2027 Godavari Pushkaralu**.
**December 2026** is the target for **R&R colonies**, not the whole project.
xa: Aug 2026: **90% civil works**, **77% overall**.
LMC up to **Visakhapatnam** also targeted for **Mar 2027**.

114.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Polavaram Project under Section 90 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Section 90 declares Polavaram a national project
Under Section 90(4), the Government of Andhra Pradesh shall execute the project and obtain all clearances
Under Section 90(3), the consent of Telangana is deemed to have been given
In practice, AP executes the irrigation component on behalf of GoI and claims reimbursement

xa: ⚠ "Which section" — answer **90**; an old key says Section **30**, some CA notes say **89** — both wrong.
Centre funds **100%** of the remaining irrigation cost from **1 April 2014**.

114.s: The Polavaram Irrigation Project was declared a national project under which section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
114.x: Section 90 declares Polavaram a national project, with the Union taking control of it, Telangana's consent deemed and the Centre executing it. Section 30 appears in an old wrong key, Section 89 concerns the KWDT reference, and Section 94 covers fiscal/industrial incentives and capital support.
xs: Polavaram was declared a national project under **Section 90** of the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014** — option **(3)**.
⚠ An old key says **Section 30** and some CA notes say **Section 89** — both wrong.
xa: **90(2)**: Union takes control of the project for **irrigation**.
**90(3)**: Telangana's consent **deemed to have been given**.
**90(4)**: **Central Government shall execute** it and obtain environmental, forest and R&R clearances.

114.s: The Left Main Canal of the Polavaram Project carries water to:
114.x: The Left Main Canal carries water to Visakhapatnam, while the Right Main Canal feeds the Krishna delta.
xa: **Revised Administrative Sanction** for the LMC came in **Jun 2026**.
LMC up to **Visakhapatnam** is targeted for **Mar 2027** (as of **15 Aug 2026**).

114.s: The Polavaram Ordinance, 2014 kept the submergence-area villages and mandals of which district with Andhra Pradesh?
114.x: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014 amended the territorial provision so that Khammam villages and mandals in the Polavaram submergence area remained with Andhra Pradesh.

AP's area rose from **1,60,205** to **1,62,970 sq km**.

xa: Centre covers **100%** of the remaining **irrigation** cost from **1 April 2014** — not drinking water or hydel.
Budget 2026-27 storage limit: **41.15 m**.
Dec 2025: expenditure **₹25,700.47 crore**; GoI advance **₹5,052.71 crore**.

Constitution of the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal

114.x: Telangana's concern is backwater at Bhadrachalam, while Odisha and Chhattisgarh objected over protective embankments.

117.x: The policy targets Net Zero by 2047, not by 2030. Its other stated features include over 160 GW of clean energy, ₹10 lakh crore investment and 7.5 lakh jobs.
117.tq: Reject the altered year in a policy target.
xs: "**Net Zero by 2030**" is wrong — option **(1)**; the policy targets **Net Zero by 2047**.
Its targets: **160 GW+** clean energy, **₹10 lakh crore** investment, **7.5 lakh jobs**.
xa: Launched **June 2024**; it absorbed the **2023 Green Hydrogen & Ammonia Policy**.
Approvals worth **₹2.88 lakh crore** (**3.47 lakh** jobs).

117.s: The AP Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy, 2023 was folded into which policy?
117.x: The 2023 green hydrogen policy was absorbed into the AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024.
xa: Targets: **160 GW+**, **₹10 lakh crore**, **7.5 lakh jobs**, **Net Zero by 2047**.
The 2023 policy was asked in **2024** (no official key published).

117.s: The Kakinada-Konaseema region is known as Andhra Pradesh's:
117.x: The Kakinada-Konaseema region is AP's oil and gas hub, associated with the KG basin.

The **Rayalaseema** industrial hub has **Kia, JSW, Royal Enfield**.

117.s:

117.s: The Andhra Pradesh Maritime Policy 2024–29 aims to make the State India's leading:
117.x: The AP Maritime Policy 2024–29 aims to make Andhra Pradesh India's leading maritime gateway.
xa: Phase-I: **+145 MTPA by 2030**; Phase-II: **300 MTPA by 2047**.
**APMB** is the nodal agency for **non-major ports**.

117.s: The AP Maritime Policy 2024-29 targets what share of all-India port cargo by 2047?
117.x: The policy targets 20% of all-India port cargo by 2047 and at least one port in the world's top 20.
xa: Capacity: **+145 MTPA by 2030** (Phase-I) and **300 MTPA by 2047** (Phase-II).
Shipbuilding: **25%** of the national target by **2047**; utilisation **75%** by 2030.
**APMB** is the nodal agency for non-major ports — SLPE with the **highest net worth**.

117.s: The nodal body for non-major ports in Andhra Pradesh is the:
117.x: The Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board is the nodal body for non-major ports in the State.
117.tq: Identify the authority responsible for the specific port category.
xs: The **AP Maritime Board (APMB)** is the nodal agency for **non-major ports** — option **(4)**.
**APIDC** (1960) is for industrial financing.
xa: APMB is the SLPE with the **highest net worth** (**₹12,600.65 crore**).
Maritime Policy aim: AP as **India's leading maritime gateway**.

117.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Industrial Corridor – Movement of goods, services and economic activity
NIMZ – Industrial development along with connectivity
Dedicated Freight Corridor – Dedicated railway freight infrastructure
Economic Corridor – Large areas with a world-class manufacturing ecosystem
117.x: A Dedicated Freight Corridor is dedicated railway freight infrastructure. An industrial corridor combines industry with connectivity, an economic corridor moves goods and services, and an NIMZ is a large manufacturing area.
n: An industrial corridor combines industrial development with connectivity. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 98-100]
A National Investment and Manufacturing Zone (NIMZ) is a large developed area with an ecosystem for world-class manufacturing. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 98-100]
An economic corridor provides connectivity that facilitates the movement of goods, services, and economic activity. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 98-100]
A Dedicated Freight Corridor is dedicated railway freight transportation infrastructure. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 98-100]

National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZs) are envisaged as large areas of developed land with the required ecosystem for world-class manufacturing. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 98-100]
xa: NIMZs are instruments of the **National Manufacturing Policy, 2011**.
AP corridors: **VCIC** (ADB-funded), **CBIC** (**Krishnapatnam** node), **HBIC** (**Orvakal** node).
AP's Industrial Policy 2024-29 prioritises links with the **East Coast DFC**.

117.s: South Coast Railway, India's 18th railway zone, is headquartered at:
117.x: SCoR is headquartered at Visakhapatnam, with Guntakal, Guntur, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam divisions; it became operational on 1 June 2026.
xa: Promised in APRA 2014's **13th Schedule**; carved from **SCR + ECoR**.
AP Industrial Policy 2024-29 prioritises **East Coast DFC** links; **Ballari-Guntakal** multi-tracking cleared (Jul 2026).

117.s: The creation of South Coast Railway was promised in which Schedule of the A.P. Reorganisation Act, 2014?
117.x: South Coast Railway was promised in the Thirteenth Schedule and carved out of the South Central and East Coast Railways.
xa: India's **18th zone**; HQ **Visakhapatnam**; operational **1 June 2026**.
APRA 2014 also asked GoI to examine a **Duggirajupatnam major port** and airport upgrades.

117.s: The Andhra Pradesh Industrial Policy 2024–29 gives priority to industrial links with:
o: Western DFC and Eastern DFC only
East Coast DFC and North–South DFC
117.x: The policy gives priority to links with the East Coast Dedicated Freight Corridor and the North–South Dedicated Freight Corridor.
117.tq: Identify the exact pair of freight corridors named in the policy.
xs: AP Industrial Policy **2024-29** prioritises **East Coast DFC + North-South DFC** links — option **(2)**.
**Bharatmala** relates to the **Raipur-Visakhapatnam** expressway, not the DFC priority.
xa: **Ballari-Guntakal** multi-tracking cleared (Jul 2026).
**VCIC** is part of **ECEC**, ADB-funded.

117.s: The Raipur–Visakhapatnam greenfield expressway is associated with which programme?
117.x: The Raipur–Visakhapatnam greenfield expressway is described as a Bharatmala economic corridor.
117.tq: Identify the responsible national infrastructure programme.
xs: The **Raipur-Visakhapatnam greenfield expressway** is a **Bharatmala** economic corridor — option **(4)**.
**East Coast DFC** is a rail freight corridor, and the **Maritime Policy** concerns ports.
xa: AP's NH network: **8,744 km**; **93** projects (**2,065 km**, **₹45,633 crore**) under way.
⚠ Do not confuse: **Bharatmala** = expressway corridor; the Industrial Policy rail priority is **East Coast DFC** + **North-South DFC**.

117.s: Bhogapuram airport became operational on:
117.x: Bhogapuram airport became operational on 1 August 2026; 1 June 2026 is when the SCoR zone became operational.
xa: APRA 2014 asked GoI to examine **Vizag/Vijayawada/Tirupati airport** upgrades.
Port limits cut under the **Indian Ports Act, 2025**.

117.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Government of India was to examine establishing a major port at:
117.x: The Act provided for examining a major port at Duggirajupatnam, a new railway zone and upgrades to the Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati airports.
xa: The railway zone became **SCoR** — India's **18th zone**, HQ **Visakhapatnam**, promised in the **13th Schedule**.
**Bhogapuram airport** became operational on **1 Aug 2026**.

117.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with an industrial-corridor node in Andhra Pradesh?
117.x: Krishnapatnam is a node on CBIC. Orvakal and Kopparthy are nodes on the Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.
117.tq: Start from the sure location–corridor pair and reject swapped corridor associations.
xs: **Krishnapatnam — CBIC** — option **(1)**.
**Orvakal** is a node of **HBIC** (Hyderabad-Bengaluru), not VCIC; Krishnapatnam is on CBIC, not HBIC.
xa: **VCIC** is part of **ECEC**, **ADB-funded**.
Industrial Policy 2024-29 prioritises **East Coast DFC** + **North-South DFC**.

117.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the four DISCOMs formed in the 2000 unbundling?
117.x: The 2000 arrangement had EPDCL-Visakhapatnam, CPDCL-Hyderabad, NPDCL-Warangal and SPDCL-Tirupati; the Vijayawada-based APCPDCL was formed later.
xa: Unbundling split **generation, transmission, distribution**.
**RDSS (2021)** replaced **UDAY (2015)**.

117.s: Which scheme, introduced in 2021, replaced UDAY in power distribution reform?
117.x: The Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), introduced in 2021, replaced UDAY (2015).
xa: Loss reduction via **smart meters** and **feeder segregation** (**312 of 3,015** feeders done).
**APEPDCL + APSPDCL** among India's top performers on loss reduction (Jan 2026).

117.s: The equity of APGIC is held by APIIC and APGENCO in the ratio:
117.x: APGIC is 51% APIIC and 49% APGENCO; it was set up on 2 September 2009 and is a partner in a KG exploration consortium.
xa: The **KG basin** (Kakinada, Konaseema) is AP's oil and gas hub.
**Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration**, Amaravati, **19 July 2025** — nodal agency **SRM University**.
AP has **no nuclear** capacity — **Kovvada** is only proposed.

117.s: In which year was APIIC incorporated?
117.x: APIIC was incorporated on 26 September 1973 and is wholly State-owned; APIDC was set up in 1960 for industrial financing and promotion.
xa: ⚠ **APIDC 1960** (financing) vs **APIIC 1973** (infrastructure).
APIIC has **25 JVs** (SES 2025-26).

117.s: The wholly State-owned APIIC mainly focuses on:
117.x: APIIC handles industrial infrastructure and land (parks, estates, SEZs, EMCs, land bank); industrial financing and promotion is APIDC's role.

Land bank: **41,998 acres**; ~**1.21 lakh acres** developed.

117.s: APIIC can allot up to how many acres of land without Cabinet approval?
117.x: APIIC can allot up to 50 acres without Cabinet approval; after 1991 its role changed from manufacturer to facilitator.
xa: APIIC was set up on **26 September 1973**; ⚠ **APIDC** (**1960**) handles industrial financing.
APIIC footprint: **635 clusters**; land bank **41,998 acres**; **25 JVs**.
APIIC is **wholly state-owned** — parks, estates, SEZs, EMCs.

117.s: The Pranahita project in the Telangana region will require 3466 MW power, almost _______ of the current total installed power generation capacity of Andhra Pradesh.

To reduce the interest payment on the Electricity sector, which scheme has been launched by the Government of India?
117.x: UDAY (Ujwal Discom Assurance Yojana), a Scheme for the financial turnaround of Power Distribution Companies (DIS- COMs), has been approved by the Government of India in November, 2015 with an objective to improve the operational and financial efficiency of the State DISCOMs. The scheme aims to reduce the interest burden, reduce the cost of power, reduce power losses in the distribution sector, rationalization of coal prices, reduction in fuel cost through coal swapping, etc. It provides permanent solutions to legacy debts of the State DISCOMs and addresses as potential future losses.

118.s: The AP Tourism Policy 2024-29 is aligned with which vision?
118.x: The policy is aligned with Swarna Andhra @2047, not Viksit Bharat @2047.
xa: Tourism + hospitality get **industry status across all segments**.

**Swarna Andhra Tourism Vision 2047** was unveiled at the **FAITH** conclave.

118.s: Under the AP Tourism Policy 2024-29, tourism and hospitality have been accorded:
o: Industry status only for Mega projects
Industry status only for heritage hotels
118.x: Tourism and hospitality got industry status across all segments, with fiscal, recurring, special and non-fiscal incentives and tailor-made packages for Mega and Ultra Mega projects.
xa: Single desk: **13** pre-establishment + **11** pre-operation clearances.
**Investment Facilitation Cell at Vijayawada**.

118.s: The AP Tourism Policy 2024-29 aims to place Andhra Pradesh among India's top ____ tourist destinations.
118.x: The policy targets a top-three rank, with tourism above 20% of State GVA and 20% of the workforce.

118.s: Budget hotels were promoted in Andhra Pradesh mainly with which objective?
o: To restrict private investment in tourism
To provide accommodation exclusively to government employees

xs: **Budget hotels** were promoted mainly **to attract tourists** — option **(1)** (APPSC G2 **2008** key).

118.x: AP is described as the birthplace of Mahayana Buddhism and has about 40 Buddhist monuments.

**Salihundam** is called the "**Tibet of AP**".

118.x: The listed Buddhist sites include Amaravati, Thotlakonda, Bavikonda, Bojjannakonda, Sankaram, Salihundam and Ghantasala. Srisailam is not included in this Buddhist-site list.

**Borra Caves** is under **Swadesh Darshan 2.0**, not CBDD.

**Simhachalam, Annavaram** are PRASHAD; **Gandikota** is SASCI; **Borra Caves** is SD 2.0.

118.x: SASCI funds Gandikota Fort and Gorge (Rs 77.91 crore) and Havelock Bridge + Pushkar ghat, Rajahmundry (Rs 94.44 crore). Borra Caves is under Swadesh Darshan 2.0 and Simhachalam/Annavaram under PRASHAD; Ahobilam and Nagarjunasagar are CBDD projects.

**Oberoi** plans a hotel at **Gandikota**.

118.s: Which beach in Andhra Pradesh has received Blue Flag recognition?
118.x: Rushikonda Beach has received Blue Flag recognition.

xs: **Rushikonda Beach** has **Blue Flag** status — option **(4)**.
**21** more beaches are proposed, **9** shortlisted.
xa: **Visakhapatnam-Bhogapuram Coastal Corridor** of **55-60 km**.
Beach-shack policy modelled on **Goa's**.

118.s: Swarna Andhra Tourism Vision 2047 was unveiled at the:

xa: Current policy: **AP Tourism Policy 2024-29**.
Tourism arrivals: **36.42 crore** (2025-26).

118.s: Which body is the fully State-owned operational arm of tourism in Andhra Pradesh, running Haritha hotels and the Srisailam ropeway?
118.x: APTDC is the State-owned operational arm running Haritha hotels, boating, sound-and-light shows and the Srisailam ropeway; PRASHAD is a Union Ministry of Tourism scheme.

PRASHAD in AP: **Simhachalam** (**₹54.04 crore**) and **Annavaram** (**₹25.32 crore**).
AP has more than **25 thematic circuits**.

118.s: The Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone (AMTZ), the medical-device hub, is located at:
118.x: AMTZ is at Visakhapatnam; Amaravati has the 'Eye Tourism' zone, AIIMS Mangalagiri anchors eSanjeevani and IITTM Nellore trains hospitality staff.

The **AstraZeneca** Genomic Solutions Centre is linked to the **Quantum Valley**.

118.s: The approved ‘Eye Tourism’ medical zone is associated with:
118.x: An Eye Tourism medical zone was approved in Amaravati.
118.tq: Test a distinctive project-location association through direct recall.
xs: The **"Eye Tourism" medical zone** is approved at **Amaravati** — option **(2)**.
**Mangalagiri** hosts AIIMS; **Visakhapatnam** hosts AMTZ; **Nellore** hosts IITTM.
xa: Amaravati also hosts **VIT, SRM, Amrita**.
Budget **2026-27**: **five regional medical hubs**.

118.s: Which of the following institutions is associated with the proposed education hub at Amaravati?
118.x: VIT, SRM and Amrita are associated with Amaravati; IIT Tirupati is not listed among the institutions hosted there.
xa: The CM wants **top world universities** in Amaravati.
Budget 2026-27: **five university townships** in industrial corridors.
**SRM University** is also nodal for the **Green Hydrogen Valley**.

118.s: In Swadesh Darshan 2.0, the sub-scheme CBDD stands for:
118.x: CBDD is Challenge Based Destination Development, a sub-scheme of Swadesh Darshan 2.0; SASCI is Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment.
xa: CBDD projects in AP: **Ahobilam** (spiritual) and **Nagarjunasagar** (heritage), **₹25 crore** each.
SASCI projects: **Gandikota** Fort and Gorge; **Havelock Bridge**, Rajahmundry.
⚠ **SD 2.0 = 52** projects; **PRASHAD = 54** projects.

118.s: Andhra Pradesh's proposed beach-shack policy is modelled on that of:
118.x: The beach-shack policy is modelled on Goa's; AP has also sought a shift of Vizag Beach Road from CRZ-3 to CRZ-2.
xa: **Rushikonda Beach** has a **Blue Flag**; **21** more proposed, **9** shortlisted.
The **55-60 km** **Visakhapatnam-Bhogapuram Coastal Corridor** is planned.
CRZ limits on Vizag beach projects are a criticism of the plan.

118.s: The Union Budget 2026–27 proposed how many regional medical hubs for medical tourism?
118.x: The Union Budget 2026–27 proposed five regional medical hubs for medical tourism, along with five university townships in industrial corridors.
xa: **AMTZ** at **Visakhapatnam** is AP's medical-device hub.
**Amaravati** hosts **VIT, SRM, Amrita**; the CM wants top world universities.

119.s:

119.x: MeeSeva training during its first year was delivered through television in partnership with MANA TV.

119.s:

B. CARD

119.s: Village and ward secretariats in Andhra Pradesh were launched on:

119.s: AP State FiberNet Ltd (APSFL), incorporated in October 2015, was launched on:

120.s: In Andhra Pradesh, a Rythu Bazar is run by:

120.s: CCRC holders can obtain all of the following without affecting the landowner's rights, EXCEPT:

**47.45%** is **Visakhapatnam**'s urbanisation; **67.35%** is AP's **literacy**.
xa: District extremes are reported across **28 districts**.
Highest literacy: **Visakhapatnam (79.05%)**.
Population share: **4.09%** (10th).

132.s: With reference to micro-irrigation implementation in 2024-25, which statement is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh ranked first, and six of its districts were in the national top ten.
Andhra Pradesh ranked first, and ten of its districts were in the national top twelve.
Andhra Pradesh ranked second, and six of its districts were in the national top ten.
Andhra Pradesh ranked third, and four of its districts were in the national top ten.
132.x: AP ranked first in micro-irrigation implementation in 2024-25, with six districts in the national top ten.
132.tq: Check both the state rank and the district count.
xs: In **micro-irrigation** (2024-25), AP ranked **first**, with **six** districts in the **national top ten** — option **(1)** is correct.
"**10 of 12**" relates to **ODOP-2024 District Awards**, not micro-irrigation.
xa: AP is also **1st** in **fruit** (**15.6%** of India) and **egg** production.
AP is **3rd** in **MGNREGS** employment (**1,635 lakh** person-days).
AP is **2nd** in **raw silk**.

132.s: Which beach in Andhra Pradesh holds the Blue Flag certification as reported in the Survey?
132.x: Rushikonda beach (Visakhapatnam) holds the Blue Flag certification. The other beaches are not the ones named as holding it.
132.tq: Blue Flag AP = Rushikonda
xs: **Rushikonda** beach holds the **Blue Flag** certification — option **(1)** is correct.
The notes do not name the other beaches.
xa: AP's coastline: **974 km** (2nd longest; **3rd** at the remeasured **1,053 km**).
AP is the leading state in fish production (about **29%**).
**ODOP-2024**: **State Award** + **10 of 12** District Awards.

132.s: According to the latest Socio-Economic Survey of Andhra Pradesh, how many Rythu Seva Kendras were functional after rationalisation?
132.x: 8,489 RSKs were functional after rationalisation. The Survey's 10,778 and 10,606 figures refer to RSKs providing soil sampling and animal husbandry services; 3,863 is the count of ward secretariats.
132.tq: Direct recall of an institutional count.
xs: **8,489** **Rythu Seva Kendras** were functional after rationalisation — option **(2)** is correct.
**10,778** (soil sampling) and **10,606** (animal husbandry) are other Survey RSK figures; **3,863** is ward secretariats.
xa: RSKs were formerly **Rythu Bharosa Kendras**.
**Fair Price Shops**: **29,796**.
**Anna Canteens**: **204** in **123** ULBs.

132.s: Stree Shakti, launched for free bus travel for women, was associated with which figures?
o: From 15 August 2025 and 33.32 crore free journeys
From 15 August 2025 and 1.84 crore free journeys
From 15 August 2024 and 33.32 lakh free journeys
132.x: Stree Shakti provided free bus travel for women from 15 August 2025 and recorded 33.32 crore free journeys.
132.tq: Match a scheme with its launch date and output figure.
xs: **Stree Shakti** runs **from 15 August 2025** with **33.32 crore free journeys** — option **(1)** is correct.
**1.84 crore** is **Deepam-2** beneficiaries; the other dates and units are wrong.
xa: It gives **free bus travel for women**.
**Anna Canteens**: **204** canteens.
⚠ crore journeys, not lakh.

132.s: The second Advance Estimates for foodgrains in Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26 placed total production at:
132.x: The 2nd Advance Estimates put 2025-26 foodgrain output at 190.29 lakh tonnes (kharif 110.00 + rabi 80.29 lakh t, up 17.03%). 47.28 lakh tonnes is fisheries output up to December 2025.
132.tq: Distinguish total foodgrains from crop-specific and allied-sector outputs.
xs: 2nd Advance Estimates 2025-26: foodgrains **190.29 lakh tonnes** — option **(2)** is correct.
**47.28 lakh tonnes** is **fisheries** output up to Dec 2025.
xa: Kharif **110.00** + rabi **80.29** lakh t, from **42.74 lakh ha**.
Output rose **17.03%**.
Rainfall (June-December 2025): **896.8 mm**, **4.2%** above normal.

132.s: As per PLFS 2023-24 (all ages), the unemployment rate of Andhra Pradesh was:
132.x: For all ages in 2023-24, AP's unemployment rate was 4.1%, with LFPR 47.5% and WPR 45.6%.
xa: Unemployment: **rural 3.4%**, **urban 5.9%**, **youth 17.5%**, **female 6.9%**.
Agriculture employs **45.6%** of workers.
⚠ **Trap**: always state the age group with the figure.

132.s: Which one of the following correctly relates the age group to the 2023-24 employment indicators reported in the SDG table?
132.x: For ages 15–59, unemployment was 4.4% and LFPR was 67.3%; these differ from the all-age figures.
132.tq: Treat the age group as part of the statistic, not as a detachable qualifier.
xs: **Ages 15–59**: unemployment **4.4%** and LFPR **67.3%** — option **(1)** is correct.
**4.1% / 47.5%** are **all-ages** PLFS figures; **5.9%** is urban unemployment.
xa: Source: APSES 2024-25 SDG table — **SDG India Index 2023-24 (SDG 8)**.
All-ages WPR: **45.6%**.
⚠ **Trap**: always state the age group with the figure.

132.s: Which one of the following correctly matches an inflation measure with the April–October 2025 figures for Andhra Pradesh and India?
132.x: In April-October 2025, CPI-IW inflation was 1.86% in Andhra Pradesh against 2.82% for India, even though AP's Combined CPI index level was higher (200.6 vs 195.9). C reverses the figures and D attaches them to CPI-AL rather than CPI-IW.
132.tq: Separate the CPI-IW and CPI-AL labels before comparing their values.
xs: **CPI-IW** inflation (April-October 2025): **1.86%** in AP vs **2.82%** in India — option **(1)** is correct.
Option 3 reverses the figures and attaches them to **CPI-AL**; option 4 uses CPI-AL instead of CPI-IW.
xa: AP's **Combined CPI** index level was still higher: **200.6** vs **195.9**.
⚠ Lower inflation rate does not mean a lower price-index level.
The Survey has a chapter on **Prices, Wages and PDS**.

132.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with Andhra Pradesh's position reported in the Survey?
o: Fish production — leading state, about 29% of India's production
132.x: Andhra Pradesh was described as the leading state in fish production, contributing about 29% of India's fish production. It ranked second in raw silk, first in micro-irrigation and sixth in exports.
132.tq: Reject swapped ranks by comparing each item with its reported position.
xs: **Fish production** — AP is the **leading state**, about **29% of India's production** — option **(1)** is correct.
AP is **2nd** (not first) in **raw silk**, **1st** (not third) in **micro-irrigation**, and **6th** (not fourth) in **exports**.
xa: ⚠ **1st** = fruit, egg, micro-irrigation; **2nd** = raw silk; **3rd** = MGNREGS; **4th** = meat; **7th** = milk.
Fisheries output: **47.28 lakh tonnes** up to Dec 2025 (**72%** of target).
Fishing and Aquaculture grew **17.69%** in 2025-26.

132.s: In NITI Aayog's Fiscal Health Index 2023-24 (released March 2026), Andhra Pradesh was ranked:
132.x: AP ranked 17th in the Fiscal Health Index 2023-24. 8th is AP's GSDP rank and 10th its population-share rank; 1st is wrong.
132.tq: FHI 2023-24: AP 17th
xs: In NITI's **Fiscal Health Index 2023-24** (Mar 2026), AP ranked **17th** — option **(3)** is correct.
**8th** is AP's **GSDP** rank; **10th** is its **population-share** rank.
xa: AP's nominal GSDP **tripled** in a decade.
Revenue deficit to widen to about **Rs 48,000 crore** in 2025-26 (AP Finance Minister).
SES 2025-26 RE puts it at **Rs 41,118 crore**.

132.s: Which region of Andhra Pradesh is being developed as a Horticulture Hub?
132.x: The Survey states that Rayalaseema is being developed as a Horticulture Hub. The other regions are not named for this.
132.tq: Horticulture hub = Rayalaseema
xs: **Rayalaseema** is being developed as a **Horticulture Hub** — option **(3)** is correct.
The notes do not name the other regions for this.
xa: AP is **1st** in **fruit production** (**15.6%** of India).
**Horticulture** has a **10%** GVA share and grew **8.78%**.
Swarnandhra-Vision KPIs include **5 horticulture KPIs**.

132.s:
Which of the following statement / statements is / are valid regarding the socio-economic status of Andhra Pradesh?
I. Andhra Pradesh won the Best State Award of ICAR-National Research Center for Banana (NRCB) for export promotion.
II. Andhra Pradesh GSDP growth rate has been registering a decline in recent times owing to repeated lower returns in certain sub-sectors of the Service Sector.
III. For the FY 2024-25, the Revenue Deficit is budgeted higher than the Fiscal Deficit in terms of percentage of Andhra Pradesh GSDP.
IV. The technology used by the Government of Andhra Pradesh while conducting resurvey of landholdings is referred to as ' Continuously Operating Stations (CORS) ' Select correct the technology. once within a period using the codes given below:
o: Only II PART-D GEOGRAPHY (Questions 91 to 120-30 Marks)
132.x: Andhra Pradesh has been recognized for agricultural exports, including banana exports promoted by ICAR-National Research Centre for Banana. The state also uses modern technologies such as Continuously Operating Reference Stations (CORS) for land resurvey and mapping.

133.s: The bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh received the President's assent on:
133.src: APPSC 2019 Various non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment

133.s: Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, for bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh received the President's assent on which day?
When was Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 for bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh received the President's assent?
133.src: APPSC 2021 Medical Officer (Ayurveda) In Ayush Department

133.s: The bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh received the President's assent on:
133.src: APPSC 2019 Various non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment

133.s: When the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 received the assent of the President?
133.src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment

133.s: The Andhra Pradesh 'Re-organization Bill' was approved and signed by the President in –
133.x: The Andhra Pradesh Re-organisation Bill 2014 was approved by the President on 1st March 2014. On 1st March 2014, the Bill was published and enacted in the Gazette. According to the Andhra Pradesh Re-organisation Act 2014, Andhra Pradesh was reorganised into 2 States (1) Andhra Pradesh and (2) Telangana.

133.s: The President's assent to the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Bill was given on:
133.x: The President gave assent on 1 March 2014, and the Act was published in Gazette No. 6 in the 65th year of the Republic.
133.tq: Separate enactment and Gazette publication from the later appointed day.
xs: The **President's assent** was given on **1 March 2014** — option **(4)** is correct.
**2 June 2014** is the **appointed day** of bifurcation.
xa: It was published in **Gazette No. 6**, in the **65th year** of the Republic.
The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha on **13 Feb 2014**.
⚠ "Came into effect on March 2, 2014" is a known wrong claim.

133.s: Under Section 85 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Krishna River Management Board has its headquarters in:
133.x: Section 85 places the KRMB in Andhra Pradesh and the Godavari River Management Board in Telangana.
xa: ⚠ **GRMB** HQ = **Telangana**; **KRMB** HQ = **AP**.
⚠ **89** = KWDT; **90** = Polavaram.
Boards were to be set up within **60 days**; security by **CISF**.

133.s: Under Section 105 of the AP Reorganisation Act, disputes over the transfer of pending cases were finally decided by:
133.x: Section 105 sent disputes on transferring pending cases to the Hyderabad High Court, whose decision was final.
xa: **Section 30**: common High Court until a separate AP HC under **Art 214**.
Judges' salaries split by **population ratio**.

133.s: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly resolution of 28 March 2026 requested that which words be inserted in Section 5(2)?
133.x: The Assembly resolution requested the insertion of the words “at Amaravati” in Section 5(2), following the High Court's order of 3 March 2022.
133.tq: Recall the exact phrase used in the legislative request.
xs: The Assembly resolution of **28 Mar 2026** sought to insert "**at Amaravati**" in **Sec 5(2)** — option **(1)** is correct.
It followed the High Court's **3 Mar 2022** order.
xa: Parliament passed the amendment in **April 2026**.
The 2026 amendment is the **first law** in which Parliament names a State's capital.
Original Sec 5: Hyderabad common capital for up to **10 years**.

133.s: Which of the following institutions is NOT included among the educational commitments in Schedule XIII?
133.x: Schedule XIII includes an IIT, NIT, IIM, IISER, Central, Petroleum and Agricultural Universities, an IIIT, an AIIMS-type hospital, a Tribal University and NIDM. An Indian Institute of Science is not listed.
133.tq: Test completeness of a named institutional list by identifying the outside institution.
xs: The **Indian Institute of Science** is **not** in the Schedule XIII education list — option **(2)** is the answer.
The list has **IIT, NIT, IIM, IISER**, Central, Petroleum and Agricultural Universities, **IIIT**, an **AIIMS-type** hospital, a **Tribal University** and **NIDM**.
xa: ⚠ **IISER** (listed) vs IISc (not listed).
The Centre must act on Schedule XIII within **10 years** (**Section 93**).
Infrastructure: **Duggirajupatnam** port.

133.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the infrastructure commitments in the Thirteenth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: The Vizag-Chennai corridor to be modelled on the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor
Feasibility study of a Vizag-Chennai industrial corridor
Feasibility study of a SAIL steel plant in Kurnool district
133.x: The SAIL steel plant feasibility study is for YSR district, not Kurnool; the Duggirajupatnam port and the DMIC-modelled Vizag-Chennai corridor study are correct.
xa: Other 6-month feasibility studies: a **refinery** and a **new railway zone**.
Section 93: measures within **10 years**.

133.s: Under Section 5 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, Hyderabad was to function as the common capital for a period of:
133.x: Section 5 provided for Hyderabad to serve as the common capital for up to ten years, after which it would be the capital of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh would have a new capital.
133.tq: Test the statutory time limit and distinguish a transitional arrangement from a permanent one.
xs: **Section 5**: Hyderabad was the **common capital for up to 10 years** — option **(4)** is correct.
Afterwards it becomes **Telangana's capital**, with a **new capital for AP**.
xa: **Section 6**: Centre to set up an **expert committee** on AP's capital within **6 months**.
**Section 8**: Governor's **special responsibility** in the common capital.
The AP Assembly (**28 Mar 2026**) sought to insert "**at Amaravati**" in **Sec 5(2)**.

133.s: Which of the following correctly describes the provisions of Sections 7 and 8?
o: They provide for the national project status of Polavaram.
They provide for the Apex Council and the two river management boards.
They provide for a common Governor and the Governor's special responsibility in the common capital.
They provide for tax incentives and capital infrastructure support.
133.x: Sections 7 and 8 deal with the common Governor and the Governor's special responsibility in the common capital.
133.tq: Identify the pair of related provisions and avoid confusing them with water or financial provisions.
xs: **Sections 7 and 8**: a **common Governor** and the **Governor's special responsibility in the common capital** — option **(3)** is correct.
Polavaram is **Section 90**; Apex Council/boards are **Sections 84-85**; tax incentives and capital support are **Section 94**.
xa: **Section 5**: Hyderabad common capital for up to **10 years**.
**Section 10**: Telangana becomes the **29th State**.
**Section 30**: common **High Court at Hyderabad**.

133.s: Section 10 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 amended the First Schedule of the Constitution to provide for Telangana as the:
133.x: Section 10 amended the First Schedule of the Constitution and recognised Telangana as the 29th State of India.
133.tq: Connect the section with the constitutional schedule and the resulting ordinal number.
xs: **Section 10** amended the **First Schedule**, making Telangana the **29th State** — option **(3)** is correct.
The other ordinal numbers are not in the notes.
xa: Telangana was formed from **10 districts** (**Section 3**).
The 2026 amendment is the **first law** in which Parliament names a State's capital.
The **Fourth Schedule** was also amended (Rajya Sabha seats).

133.s: The Apex Council constituted under Section 84 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 is chaired by the:
o: Chief Ministers of both States jointly
133.x: The Apex Council is chaired by the Union Water Resources Minister, with the Chief Ministers of both States as members.
xa: **Section 85**: **GRMB** (HQ **Telangana**) and **KRMB** (HQ **AP**) within **60** days.
Schedule XI: no new Krishna/Godavari project without **Apex Council** sanction.
Board security: **CISF**.

133.s: Under which Section of the A.P. Reorganisation Act, 2014 was the Polavaram Irrigation Project declared a national project?
133.x: Section 90 declared Polavaram a national project, with Telangana's consent deemed given. Section 84 is the Apex Council, Section 89 extends the KWDT term (a common wrong answer), and Section 93 deals with Thirteenth Schedule measures.
xs: **Section 90** declared **Polavaram** a **national project**, with **Telangana's consent deemed given** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Section 84** = Apex Council; **Section 89** = KWDT term extension; **Section 93** = Thirteenth Schedule measures.
xa: ⚠ **89** = KWDT; **90** = Polavaram — a common trap.
The **Polavaram Ordinance** amended **Sec 3** to keep the **Khammam** submergence villages with AP.
**Section 91**: Tungabhadra Board arrangements.

133.s: Under Section 30 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the High Court at Hyderabad was to remain common until:
o: The Governor of Telangana issued a notification
The expiry of ten years from the appointed day, irrespective of any new High Court
A separate High Court for Andhra Pradesh was set up under Article 214
The new State capitals were finalised by Parliament
133.x: The Hyderabad High Court remained common to both States until a separate High Court for Andhra Pradesh was established under Article 214.
133.tq: Identify the legal condition that ends a transitional institutional arrangement.
xs: **Section 30**: the **High Court at Hyderabad** stayed common **until a separate AP High Court was set up under Art 214** — option **(3)** is correct.
It was not tied to a fixed ten-year period or a Governor's notification.
xa: Judges' salaries were split by **population ratio**.
The Act named **no place** for AP's High Court.
**Section 105**: pending-case transfer disputes go to the **Hyderabad High Court**, whose decision is **final**.

133.s: Which provision of Section 94 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 is correctly matched?
o: Section 94(2) – Special support for the new capital
Section 94(3) – Denotification of degraded forest land
Section 94(1) – Fiscal measures including tax incentives
133.x: 94(1) covers fiscal measures, 94(2) backward-area infrastructure, 94(3) special support for the new capital and 94(4) denotification of degraded forest land.
xa: **Section 46** gives a special development package for **Rayalaseema and North Coastal AP**.
**Section 93**: Thirteenth Schedule measures within **10 years**.

133.s: How were the salaries of judges of the common High Court dealt with under the reorganisation provisions?
o: They were divided according to the population ratio.
They were equally divided between the Union and the two States.
They were borne entirely by Andhra Pradesh.
They were borne entirely by Telangana.
133.x: The salaries of the judges of the common High Court were divided according to the population ratio.
133.tq: Test the precise basis of financial allocation rather than the identity of the paying authority.
xs: Judges' salaries of the common High Court were **divided according to the population ratio** — option **(1)** is correct (**Section 30**).
The notes do not say the cost was split equally or borne by one State.
xa: The common High Court lasted until a separate AP HC under **Art 214**.
**Section 46** also uses **population ratio** to split the **13th FC** award.
The Act named **no place** for AP's High Court.

133.s: Which Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 deals with the allotment of sitting members of the Rajya Sabha?
133.x: The First Schedule provides for allotment of sitting Rajya Sabha members and is linked with Section 13.
133.tq: Use the schedule number and its associated legislative subject as a direct recall pair.
xs: **Schedule I** of the Act: **allotment of sitting Rajya Sabha members** (**Sec 13**) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Schedule II** = Delimitation Order 2008 amendments; **Schedule III** = Council constituencies; **Schedule IV** = Council members.
xa: ⚠ Do not confuse with the Constitution's **Fourth Schedule** (Rajya Sabha seats: AP **11**, Telangana **7**).
**Schedule VII** = **List of Funds** (asked in APPSC 2022).
**Schedule VIII** = apportionment of **pension** liability (Sec 59).

133.s: Under Schedule XII of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the State Load Despatch Centre was shared for up to:
133.x: The SLDC was shared for up to two years, while APERC acted as a joint regulator for up to six months.
xa: **APGENCO** units were divided by **location**.
Power is under **Schedule XII** (**Coal, Oil and Gas, Power**).
⚠ APERC **6 months** vs SLDC **2 years**.

133.s:
Assertion (A): After reorganisation, Andhra Pradesh has 25 Lok Sabha seats and Telangana has 17.
Reason (R): Andhra Pradesh has 175 Legislative Assembly seats and Telangana has 119.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
133.x: Both seat distributions are correct (Lok Sabha 25 and 17; Assembly 175 and 119), but the Assembly figures do not explain the Lok Sabha figures.
xa: Totals: RS **18**, LS **42**, Assembly **294**.
Council: AP **not more than 50**, Telangana **40**.
**Section 26**: AP Assembly can rise from 175 to **225**, subject to **Art 170**.

133.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, which Schedules of the Constitution were amended?
133.x: Section 10 amended the First Schedule, while the Fourth Schedule was amended to revise the Rajya Sabha representation of Andhra Pradesh and provide an entry for Telangana.
133.tq: Recall the exact constitutional Schedules rather than confusing them with Articles or statutory Schedules.
xs: The Act amended the **First and Fourth Schedules** of the Constitution — option **(3)** is correct (**APPSC 2021** answer).
**First Schedule** (Sec 10): Telangana added; **Fourth Schedule**: Rajya Sabha seats — AP **18 → 11**, Telangana **7**.
xa: **Art 168(1)(a)** amended to add Telangana's Legislative Council (**Sec 96**).
**Art 371D** now reads "**Andhra Pradesh or Telangana**" (**Sec 97**).
**RPA 1950** First Schedule was amended for Lok Sabha seats.

133.s: Which constitutional provision was amended to include Telangana among the States having a Legislative Council?
133.x: Section 96 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act amended Article 168(1)(a) to add Telangana to the States with a Legislative Council.
133.tq: Match the constitutional Article with the specific institutional change.
xs: **Article 168(1)(a)** was amended (**Sec 96**) to add Telangana to States with a **Legislative Council** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Art 170** relates to Assembly delimitation (Sec 26); **Art 333** relates to Anglo-Indian nomination (Sec 18).
xa: Council seats: AP **not more than 50**; Telangana **40**.
**RPA 1951** Sec **15A** was amended for the Telangana Council (**Sec 98**).
**Schedule IV** of the Act lists Legislative Council members (Sec 22).

133.s: After the amendment made by the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, Article 371D refers to:
133.x: Section 97 amended Article 371D so that it reads “Andhra Pradesh or Telangana.”
133.tq: Test the precise wording of the amended constitutional provision.
xs: After **Sec 97**, **Art 371D** reads "**Andhra Pradesh or Telangana**" — option **(2)** is correct.
So it does not refer to AP alone or Telangana alone.
xa: **Sec 96** amended **Art 168(1)(a)** (Telangana Council).
**Sec 10** amended the **First Schedule**.
The **SC and ST Orders 1950** were also amended (**Schedules V / VI**).

133.s: The First Schedule of which enactment was amended in relation to Lok Sabha seats following the reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh?
133.x: The First Schedule of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 was amended for the allocation of Lok Sabha seats. The Representation of the People Act, 1951 was amended separately through Section 15A for the Telangana Legislative Council.
133.tq: Discriminate between the two Representation of the People Acts and their respective amendments.
xs: The **First Schedule** of the **Representation of the People Act, 1950** was amended for **Lok Sabha seats** — option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC 2021** answer).
**RPA 1951** was amended separately (**Sec 15A**, for the Telangana Council, via **Sec 98**).
xa: Other laws amended: **Delimitation Order 2008**; **SC and ST Orders 1950**; **States Reorganisation Act 1956** Sec 15.
Lok Sabha seats: AP **25**, Telangana **17**.
⚠ RPA **1950** = seats; RPA **1951** = elections/Council.

133.s: Under Section 26 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the strength of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly could be raised from 175 to:
133.x: Section 26 permitted the possibility of increasing Andhra Pradesh's Assembly strength from 175 to 225, subject to Article 170 of the Constitution.
133.tq: Use the before-and-after numerical pair and retain the constitutional condition.
xs: **Section 26**: delimitation can raise AP's Assembly from **175 to 225** — option **(3)** is correct.
This is **subject to Art 170**.
xa: Telangana's Assembly: **119** seats; combined total **294**.
**Section 18**: each Governor could nominate **1 Anglo-Indian** MLA (**Art 333**).
**Schedule II** amends the **Delimitation Order, 2008** (Sec 15).

133.s: Section 18 of the AP Reorganisation Act allowed each Governor to nominate one Anglo-Indian MLA under Article:
133.x: Section 18 provided for one nominated Anglo-Indian member in each Assembly under Article 333 (the provision was later ended by the 104th Amendment).
xa: **Section 26**: AP Assembly can rise from **175** to **225** (Art 170).
Telangana Assembly: **119** seats.
AP Council: **not more than 50** seats.

133.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Eleventh Schedule — Coal, oil and gas and power
Eighth Schedule — Government companies and corporations
Ninth Schedule — Apportionment of pension liability
Tenth Schedule — Continuance of facilities in State institutions
133.x: The Tenth Schedule concerns continuance of facilities in State institutions, such as APSCHE and Shilparamam. The Eighth concerns pension liability, the Ninth concerns companies and corporations, and the Eleventh concerns river management boards.
133.tq: Check the order of closely related schedules and identify the correctly matched pair among deliberate swaps.
xs: **Tenth Schedule — continuance of facilities in State institutions** is correct (e.g., **APSCHE**, **Shilparamam**) — option **(4)**.
**Eleventh** = **river boards** (not coal/power); **Eighth** = **pension** liability (not companies).
**Coal, Oil and Gas, Power** is the **Twelfth** Schedule.
xa: ⚠ **VII** = Funds; **VIII** = pension; **XI** = river boards; **XII** = coal/oil/power; **XIII** = education & infrastructure.
**Schedules V / VI**: amendments to the **SC and ST Orders 1950**.

133.s: Which Schedule lays down the principles for the Godavari and Krishna River Management Boards?
133.x: Schedule XI contains the principles for the Godavari and Krishna River Management Boards.
133.tq: Link the two named river boards to their common schedule rather than to the water-resources Part alone.
xs: **Schedule XI** sets the principles for the **Godavari and Krishna River Management Boards** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Schedule XII** = coal, oil and gas, power; **Schedule X** = continuance of facilities in institutions.

xs: Loans instead of grants raise **repayment burdens** and **crowd out welfare and development** spending — option **(3)**.
They do not stop private investment or remove audits.
AP's projected debt is **Rs 7.11 lakh crore** (about **36%** of GSDP).

139.s: The Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) of NITI Aayog was launched in :
139.x: Launched by the PM Narendra Modi in January 2018, the Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) of NITI Aayog aims to quickly and effectively transform 112 most under-developed districts across the country. With States as the main drivers, this programme focuses on the strength of each district, identifying low-hanging fruits for immediate improvement and measuring progress by ranking districts on a monthly basis. The ranking is based on the incremental progress made across 49 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) under 5 broad socio-economic themes– Health & Nutrition, Education, Agriculture & Water Resources, Financial Inclusion & Skill Development and Infrastructure. PM Modi launched the Aspirational Blocks Programme (ABP) of NITI Aayog in January, 2023, aiming to expedite the development of 500 relatively underdeveloped blocks across the country and improve socio-economic conditions in them.

142.s: Under the Thirteenth Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Government of India was required to examine the feasibility of which industrial corridor within six months?

xs: The **Thirteenth Schedule** asks GoI to examine the **Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor** within **six months** — so option **(4)** is correct.

The same Act asks GoI to **take steps** for **rapid rail and road connectivity** from AP's new capital to **Hyderabad** and other Telangana cities.
The State law for corridors is the **A.P. Industrial Corridor Development Authority Act, 2017**, which creates **AP-ICDA**.

142.s: The Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor was proposed to be developed on the lines of which corridor?

**CBIC** and the **Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor** are fellow AP corridors, not the template.
xa: Exam trio: VCIC **funded by ADB**, **part of ECEC**, **modelled on DMIC**.

xs: **CBIC** (Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor) has Japanese (**JICA**) support — so option **(1)** is correct.
**VCIC** is **ADB**-funded (**$840 mn** programme); notes naming JICA for VCIC are a conflict — follow ADB.

142.s: Of the $840 million Vizag–Chennai Industrial Corridor programme, the Asian Development Bank's share is:

142.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the seven high-speed rail corridors identified as “growth connectors” in the Union Budget 2026–27?

**World Bank and ADB** are named for **Amaravati capital loans**, not APFAMGS.

142.s: In the Union Budget 2024-25, the GOI has promised funds to which industrial nodes as part of the Vishakhapatnam-Chennai and Bangalore- Hyderabad industrial corridors?
